Google review of Whole Foods Market (5 out of 5, by Melanie E, 3 months ago): Food: 5/5 I came here to buy some drinks, yogurt, and fruit. I didn't try any of their prepared foods. I found their fruits and vegetables were fresh.

Service: 4/5 one staff member was helpful in finding the item for me. They have several self serve checkout counters.

Atmosphere: 5/5 place is nice and clean. There are two floors and the lower floor had a big eating area.

Bakery and sandwich to-go selection pretty sparse. It felt crammed and confined but most NYC grocery stores do to someone from California.

The staff is welcoming and friendly, when I pick up the Chefs dinner the Chef really hooks it up. I’m on a high protein diet and appreciate the generous portions. The salad bar is always well stocked and organized & the coffee shop is awsome. The almond croissants are addictive ‼️

Cool experience today. The butchers are samurai, at this location.

Google review of Whole Foods Market (1 out of 5, by Marc Posneck, 8 months ago): WholeFoods Tribeca, how about respecting New York law and NOT LETTING DOGS IN YOUR STORE?
I shop there every day and every day I see many dogs that obviously are not service animals. No one ask the inconsiderate dog owners for justification so they all get in with their dogs. As a result, you can see dogs sniffing groceries, barking at customers, putting their paws on food displays, and even peeing - true, see the picture. It's DISGUSTING and totally UNHYGIENIC.
RESPECT THE LAW and make sure dogs stay out of your store.

docs.title: Review of Whole Foods Market
docs.text:
Google review of Whole Foods Market (1 out of 5, by tanisha colon, 3 months ago): Staff needs consistent training or if discretion is going to be used it should be used in a fair, consistent manner. I am quite perturbed that I visited this store for the 1st time on Friday,  June 19, 2026 around 11:45am--12:15 pm. We (2 adults, and 2 children) were on our way to nearby park and stopped to get bottled water. Instead of grabbing bottle water from food truck I said let me come instead and grab Alkaline water and large size that I always get from WholeFoods.

The store is huge, and it was a maze to get to register. When we inquired as to register a staff member directed us to walk near/down aisle 12, however, we then spotted the customer service desk. There were no customers there that the Rep, an older female employee, was assisting so I walked up and asked if I could pay for our bottled waters here she said, "no, I am sorry I cannot ring up products here, I can only do returns" I said ma'am I have shopped at many of whole foods and customer service can certainly ring up a customer with a few items. I was annoyed and disappointed, as this interaction was not accommodating and wasted more time in our quest to find the register.

While I did not go back and forth with the woman or even call for a manager as the children were anxious to get to the park, what truly annoyed me and caused me to write this review, is that upon us existing the store, we passed the customer service desk, and proceeded to watch this same employee ring up a man paying for a water/beverage. I was really annoyed but proceeded to exist.

I am bringing this up as it is not fair, consistent and definitely the level of customer service I am accustomed to shopping at a market, certainly not a market the caliber of Whole Foods. I hope the Manager looks into this and speaks to this woman. What made matters worst is that as I mentioned the store is huge, and we needed that accommodation to pay in a quick manner versus walking through the entire store to reach the register, as we had a child with us that has a disability.

docs.title: Review of Whole Foods Market
docs.text:
Google review of Whole Foods Market (5 out of 5, by jack coffey, 4 months ago): Whole Foods has become one of my favorite places to stop during my lunch break. Like most people, I could easily grab something quick and head back to work, but what makes this location stand out is that it offers a comfortable place to actually sit down, eat, and take a few minutes to recharge before getting back to the day.

The food selection is excellent. Whether I’m looking for something healthy, a hot meal, a sandwich, soup, salad, or just a quick snack, there always seems to be plenty of fresh options available. The quality is consistently good, and I appreciate that I can find meals that don’t leave me feeling weighed down for the rest of the afternoon.

One feature I particularly like is the eating area. Having a dedicated space where you can sit comfortably and enjoy your meal makes a bigger difference than people might think. It turns a rushed lunch into an actual break. I’ve spent many lunch hours there reading, planning out the rest of my day, or simply relaxing for a few minutes before heading back to work.

The store itself is clean, well-organized, and easy to navigate. The staff has always been friendly and helpful whenever I’ve needed assistance.

Overall, Whole Foods offers much more than groceries. For me, it’s become a reliable lunch destination with good food, a comfortable atmosphere, and a welcome break from the workday. Five stars.

docs.text:
Google review of Whole Foods Market (5 out of 5, by moises acosta, a year ago): The pizza here is surprisingly good. The food bar itself is top quality. One of the best Whole Foods in the city. Very large layout. Endless organic products.
Great location too by WTC, financial district, and hudson river park.

docs.title: Review of Whole Foods Market
docs.text:
Google review of Whole Foods Market (1 out of 5, by Jason Ikeler, 5 months ago): Great delivery from Whole Foods, super clean and professional. The driver even gave us a bonus surprise gift of broken glass and marinara sauce left all over the floor in front of our apartment door.

The E-Commerce staff was somehow even better. We called about the broken jar and the 5 missing items, and were told there was basically nothing they could do because the guy on the phone was absolutely certain none of it was his fault. Love that positive attitude!

docs.title: Review of Happier Grocery
docs.text: Google review of Happier Grocery (5 out of 5, by Yael Sananes, a month ago): Such a happy place!! you can find fresh vegetables and fruits all over the place cheese, yogurts, supplements and ever she and everything is super fresh and inviting. There is also a popular coffee stand, but I didn’t try it. You can find people buying coffee from this place all day long.

docs.title: Review of Happier Grocery
docs.text: Google review of Happier Grocery (5 out of 5, by Matilde, 5 months ago): This store is crazy but definitely funny to explore. I saw people actually doing grocery here which is even fun to witness. You can definitely find some stuff on the cheaper side (like 3-10$). But the fun stuff is just to explore and see how crazy America can get over food (I bought fermented cashews????)

docs.title: Review of Happier Grocery
docs.text:
Google review of Happier Grocery (3 out of 5, by Eva Baur, 7 months ago): Super cute and very aesthetic grocery store. Everything looks beautiful and carefully curated, so it’s definitely fun to walk around and browse. That said, I honestly don’t understand how anyone could shop here regularly. The prices are easily 3x what you’d normally pay, and not in a way that feels justified.

Portions are also really small, and the overall vibe feels very niche with a pretty specific clientele. For me it ended up feeling a bit like an aesthetic rip-off — nice to look at, but hard to take seriously as an actual grocery store.

docs.title: Review of Happier Grocery
docs.text: Google review of Happier Grocery (3 out of 5, by Lexi Bennett, a year ago): I have a conflicted review. As someone with a ton of food allergies, this place was a dream. SO many options, especially gluten free. I was super excited and it was like eye candy to look at all the fun brands they had. However, almost all of the food disappointed me. Expensive and not very expensive-tasting. The thing I enjoyed most was from Sixteen Mill Bakeshop, so it wasn’t exactly from Happier Grocery. However, the staff was very kind!! It’s also a beautiful place in a great location. Overall, I’d definitely come back, but I wouldn’t choose to have my whole meal here

docs.title: Review of Happier Grocery
docs.text: Google review of Happier Grocery (3 out of 5, by Brenda Sanchez, 3 months ago): The food is good, but nothing overly special. A small plate with just chicken and potatoes will run you for 33$, while not even being a full portion. Overall though the ambiance and organization is nice, but be weary if your on a tighter budget.

docs.title: Review of Hong Kong Supermarket
docs.text:
Google review of Hong Kong Supermarket (5 out of 5, by Chaeim chacham, a year ago): If you are a fan of exotic foods and looking for a unique culinary experience, the "Hong Kong" supermarket in New York is definitely worth a visit. The store offers an impressive selection of Asian products, including rare fruits and vegetables that are hard to find in regular supermarkets.

The variety is remarkable – you will find tropical fruits, exotic vegetables, and unique spices suitable for a wide range of Asian cuisines. Additionally, there is a rich selection of ready-to-eat foods, authentic sauces, and essential ingredients for traditional Chinese, Japanese, and Thai cooking.

The store is well-organized, making it easy to navigate, although it can get a bit crowded, especially during peak hours. Prices vary – some items may be slightly more expensive compared to regular supermarkets, but given their quality and uniqueness, the shopping experience is well worth it.

In summary, "Hong Kong" is a must-visit destination for anyone who enjoys exploring new flavors and discovering high-quality Asian products. If you are looking to try something new or bring a taste of Asian cuisine home, this is the place for you.

docs.title: Review of Jubilee Marketplace
docs.text: Google review of Jubilee Marketplace (5 out of 5, by Thomas, 4 months ago): Amazing supermarket with good food. We had nearly everyday the cheap bagels with salmon, egg/cheese/bacon or cream cheese - everything was delicious. Coffee for 1,50$ - great for breakfast. The supermarket itself was also good and cheaper then the other. Staff was friendly.

docs.title: Review of Jubilee Marketplace
docs.text: Google review of Jubilee Marketplace (5 out of 5, by LeGrod, 10 months ago): Popped in here while looking for something easy to have for lunch, and what a surprise it was! Great spread of food options, we tried a little bit of almost everything, and were very happy with all of it. Price was pretty good especially at the $9.99 a pound, but be prepared to run out of space in your container trying to grab some of it all. They had a large variety of packaged ramen and other Korean foods throughout the store too. A very clean place with fair prices overall, will definitely be back to try out more food from the buffet

docs.title: Review of Jubilee Marketplace
docs.text:
Google review of Jubilee Marketplace (5 out of 5, by Krishin Asnani, 2 months ago): I remember this place as one I arrived at  post business meetings where I tried to convince Wall Street clients to get internet connections back in the mid 90s; they had a seating area where I discussed the lies we told clients about our products.

But there is no seating area now!  Worse it’s not longer a convivial, family owned bodega with a social function;  it is now a mini supermarket with a bouncer ;

Perhaps  it should become a dance club as the name Jubilee and the bouncer fits that business far more.

docs.text:
Google review of Dumbo Market (5 out of 5, by Filiz Keskin, 2 months ago): I had such a great experience at Dumbo Market today! It was pouring rain outside, and the staff went above and beyond by kindly offering me an umbrella. That small gesture meant so much.

A special thank you to Adele and Yusuf for being so friendly, thoughtful, and genuinely caring. Excellent customer service like this is hard to find these days, and they made my day. I’ll definitely be coming back. Highly recommend this place!

docs.title: Review of Dumbo Market
docs.text:
Google review of Dumbo Market (4 out of 5, by Fred Alluso, a year ago): Very nice market. It is quite late and they truly seem to be carrying a little of everything.

As you enter the store you will find the produce straight ahead, and a very good cafe and dining area on your right.

The coffee, espresso, and cappuccino are better and less expensive than the big green shop across the street. Great service at a great price. They also bake their own pastries.

Google review of Kam Man Market (5 out of 5, by Yin Lau, a year ago): If you're in Chinatown, New Kam Man Supermarket on Canal Street is a must-visit for anyone who loves Asian food and culture. It’s not just any market—New Kam Man holds the distinction of being the first Chinese supermarket in the United States.

The front roast meat counter is a neighborhood favorite. Grab a box of one or two meats over rice for just $9—crispy roast pork, char siu, soy sauce chicken—hot, flavorful, and perfect for an easy lunch or no-cook dinner.

Inside, you'll find a treasure trove of Asian snacks, from Korean chips to Japanese treats that are cheaper than at most Japanese convenience stores in Manhattan. It's easy to get lost in the aisles of goodies.

Downstairs, explore an impressive assortment of Chinese teas. If you're lucky, Mr. Chen, the owner, might be there to walk you through which teas help with digestion, sleep, or boosting energy. It’s like stepping into a living encyclopedia of tea culture.

Home chefs will appreciate the wall of high-quality knives, steamers, and kitchen tools, plus shelves stocked with every Asian condiment you could imagine—soy sauce, chili crisp, fish sauce, black vinegar, and more.

New Kam Man is more than a supermarket—it’s a hub for food, culture, and history. Whether you’re shopping for ingredients, grabbing a quick meal, or just soaking in the atmosphere, it’s Chinatown at its finest.

docs.title: Review of Kam Man Market
docs.text: Google review of Kam Man Market (5 out of 5, by John Gonsalves, a year ago): Kam Man Market in Chinatown is a great spot if you're looking for a wide variety of Chinese products all in one place. They have everything from snacks and sauces to kitchenware and teas. One of the highlights is definitely the fresh roasted meats—everything from duck to pork, and it all smells amazing as soon as you walk in. It’s a solid go-to if you’re stocking up on Chinese groceries or just want something freshly made to eat.

docs.title: Review of Kam Man Market
docs.text:
Google review of Kam Man Market (5 out of 5, by Bonnie Tran, a year ago): I stopped by Kam Man Market today and found many items that helped me make small but noticeable improvements to my kitchen and organization.

Everyone knows how that could be with a growing family. I invested in some higher quality dinner utensils I was unable to find elsewhere for the same price. Most vendors sell them in larger sets but here I was able to tailor it to my needs. I also found some large porcelain soup spoons. Perfect for when we have soup noodles at home.

Also a very unique rack that served perfectly for my bamboo cutting board (a gift) and chopsticks. It keeps the cutting board lifted to dry and free from mold and also keeps the chopsticks from falling to the side which happens all too often. A very ergonomic design I haven’t seen in all my shopping at other vendors.

I bought a little dust pan and brush for minor countertop messes I make from scooping formula repeatedly. And an affordable thermos for trips with the baby.

Also, if youre looking to clean the lime or residue from your hot water dispenser it’s here! I tried to order it from Amazon and it took so long from Japan they canceled it. I was very surprised to see it here.

Finally I also saw metalic exercise balls for the hand that I haven’t in many years. I quickly added it to my basket along with incense. after buying I also saw that it is perfect for meditation and relaxation as well.

I quickly integrated these items to my new home and they all work great. I’m pleased with my purchases and was not disappointed. I will continue to add to my collection from their wide assortment of dinnerware. Again all at competitive prices!

docs.text:
Google review of Tan Tin Hung Supermarket (5 out of 5, by Ruby Chan, a month ago): Tan Tin Hung (信興) is only a 3-minute walk from Grand St station and has all kinds of Vietnamese snacks, like bánh da lợn, khoai mì nướng, and bánh xu xê.

The nem chua is $10 and comes individually wrapped in plastic. it’s a Vietnamese fermented cured pork sausage that kind of tastes like salami! It’s topped with garlic and chili, with coarse black pepper mixed in, so it has a pretty spicy kick.

They also carry a pretty big selection of Southeast Asian groceries. FYI they’re closed on Thursdays.

docs.title: Review of Stage Door Delicatessen
docs.text: Google review of Stage Door Delicatessen (5 out of 5, by Jenna North, 3 months ago): My daughter and I looked for some breakfast places in FiDi.  I had ate at the pizzeria upstairs but not the deli.  We decided on this deli because the menu was so full.   A lot of the places in the area have some breakfast items but not a full menu. The food was fantastic.  We were floored that the strawberry cream cheese had actual strawberries.  Eggs were perfectly over medium. The potatoes reminded me of the ones my dad used to make when I was growing up! Such nostalgia! The place wasn’t super busy.  We ordered, walked to register to pay, and food was ready.  Great prices. The service was impeccable.  Everyone was super friendly and personable.  Made us feel like friends and not just customers. Well worth a visit for good food, great prices and friendly service!

docs.title: Review of Stage Door Delicatessen
docs.text: Google review of Stage Door Delicatessen (3 out of 5, by Harry Zhang, 4 months ago): Very surprised by how good the food is. One of the biggest à la carte menu I’ve ever seen, and by such a small kitchen. The spot has been a NYC staple since 1966. Now my go-to spot for a healthy and delicious meal that hit the spot that won’t break the bank.

docs.title: Review of Stage Door Delicatessen
docs.text: Google review of Stage Door Delicatessen (5 out of 5, by Todd Jobson, II, 4 months ago): This is a hidden gem in the financial district. The pizza shop upstairs is the real deal. Their slices are thin, crispy, and packed with flavor. They have great, doughy garlic knots too. Considering the location, prices are pretty reasonable as well.

docs.title: Review of Stage Door Delicatessen

Staff were great, wonderful friendly service.
Cheap and easy setup for good value quick food not a premium dining experience.

docs.title: Review of Stage Door Delicatessen
docs.text: Google review of Stage Door Delicatessen (5 out of 5, by Nikki W, 9 months ago): As soon as we walked in, they directed us where to order and pay. I got a bagel with strawberry cream cheese (I think it was plain cream cheese with strawberry puree and it was delicious). I picked up a banana and juice too, and it was under $10. We ate in and it was very comfortable in there. Would highly recommend. We went around 8:30am on a Saturday and it wasn’t busy.

docs.title: Review of Open Market
docs.text: Google review of Open Market (5 out of 5, by Rafael Conejos, 2 years ago): Well priced, diverse buffet, delicious! I grew up in Asia and the Asian selection is pretty good! Also the sushi is well priced. But their sandwiches are epic too. It isn't Katz deli but their pastrami us alright for the price. Everyone working are also pretty chill and friendly, from the guy making sandwiches, to the crew manning the cashier. Also, very clean eating area and bathroom.

docs.title: Review of Open Market
docs.text: Google review of Open Market (5 out of 5, by Dane, 7 years ago): You’ve got everything you could ever hope for in his place... tacos, stir fry, sushi, burgers, a salad bar, soups, ramen.. a buffet style bar.. I mean you name it they’ve got it. Sure it gets very crowded around lunch time but that’s to be expected at a place like this and the lines move very quickly. Never have more than a 10 minute wait. The prices are on the higher side of things but I don’t mind too much since everything is fresh and often prepared right in front of you. Plenty of space of dine inside or outside if you please. The place is well lit and clean and staff is friendly and helpful. Probably my number one go to lunch spot. Thanks Open Market... see you soon!

docs.title: Review of Open Market
docs.text:
Google review of Open Market (4 out of 5, by Joaquín Núñez, 3 years ago): If you’re a tourist in NYC with a tight budget: this deli is a healthy and affordable option to have lunch. Good quality food and service. They have several options.

The lasagna was very tasty and fresh, the grilled salmon was great and the greens are greens.

Plus is very close to Wall Street, metro stations and other attractions.

docs.title: Review of Open Market
docs.text: Google review of Open Market (4 out of 5, by Luna Martínez, 3 years ago): Good spot to grab a quick meal during lunch break. They have a salad bar and a hot food bar with some staples and some different options every day, including vegan and vegetarian options. There’s a wide selection of nonalcoholic drinks in the shopping area, from juice and kombucha to soda and flavored water. Prices are comparable to others in the area.

docs.text:
Google review of Regina's Grocery (5 out of 5, by Bella Teebagy, a year ago): I LOVE THIS SPOT & you will too!!!

This place is hands down authentic Italian food, its THE place to get a sub. To start, the people, the service, was super friendly, and always is because I've been here numerous of times. Also, this just so happens to be my favorite location. It definitely gives hole-in-the-wall vibes but trust me when I say trust the process. The first time I ever went, someone was boasting about how good the chicken cutlet sandwich was. I didn't order it, but still, both my friend and I's food was hands down amazing. We sat at the single table they ave for seating, that seats two!

I got the Ricky sandwich and my friend got Cousin Anthony which again, both amazing. Fresh and even when I ate the other half 4 hours later, unrefrigerated, and through the pouring rain, it was somehow still perfect. Whenever I'm in the area, I will always be a loyal customer (:

docs.text: Google review of Regina's Grocery (4 out of 5, by Brody Helms, a year ago): I came here to look at the products available to purchase. I also ordered some canolis. They were filled with a vanilla filling. I have had many cannoli before and these were definitely up there. The cannoli was crunchy and not soggy. The filling was just the right amount of sweetness. I definitely want to go back to try some of the other menu items as well. What makes this location great is that it is right next to a good pizza place.

docs.title: Review of The Best Of New York Food
docs.text:
Google review of The Best Of New York Food (5 out of 5, by Christina Drew, a year ago): Service: The gentleman at the counter was so very nice and accommodating, wow! He gave us some awesome recommendations and chatted with us about the menu, then brought is everything we needed to accompany our meal. Really nice guy! He even invited us back for coffee the next morning. 10/10

Food: 100/10 - let’s start there. We ordered Chopped Cheese, SEC on a plain bagel, fries, tots and pancakes. The food is made to order - so fresh and piping hot. We also got bottled 3 drinks and our total was about $53. I’m not sure if that’s considered pricey or not, but it was worth it to us.

Location/Atmosphere: 10/10 it’s in an easy to find location, clean and they have space to host your meal inside the deli. I love that so much. Everything was adding to the real New York experience. Loved it!

The staff is also lovely and helpful. Stop by you won’t regret it!

docs.title: Review of Champs Gourmet Deli
docs.text: Google review of Champs Gourmet Deli (4 out of 5, by Sunny, 2 years ago): I had a great meal at Champs Gourmet Deli on 30 Broad St, NY. I ordered the meal of the day, which included beans, rice, pork sausages with onions, and boiled vegetables. The sausage was the highlight—probably the best I've ever had. The chicken soup was also flavorful, and it’s hard to find a meal like this for under $20 in the financial district. While the atmosphere could have been slightly better, everything else was spot on. I’ll definitely be back whenever I’m in the area.

docs.text:
Google review of West Bank Gourmet Deli in Battery Park (5 out of 5, by Richard Toth, a year ago): The gentleman and the lady behind the counter are always so warm, friendly, and welcoming. It makes such a difference to be greeted with genuine kindness every time you walk in.

Their coffee is absolutely fantastic, rich, smooth, and honestly better than most of the big-name high street brands.

The food is just as impressive. Portions are generous, everything is fresh, and the prices are fair. Whether you’re grabbing breakfast, lunch, or just a quick snack, you get great value and consistently good taste.

Highly recommend stopping by if you’re in the neighborhood. This place feels like a true local favorite for a reason!

Google review of Shinjuku Japanese Deli (5 out of 5, by dong zeng, 10 months ago): Nestled in the city’s hustle and bustle, this convenience store redefines "on-the-go living" with its exquisite ingenuity and thoughtful curation. Unlike ordinary outlets, every corner here holds subtle surprises—sleek, minimalist shelves display a curated mix of artisanal snacks, premium beverages, and practical essentials, seamlessly blending functionality with taste.

The quality of its offerings truly stands out: freshly brewed specialty coffee boasts a rich, aromatic profile that rivals boutique cafes; ready-to-eat meals are crafted with meticulous care—juicy teriyaki chicken rice bowls with perfectly seasoned grains, crisp salad boxes tossed in house-made dressings, and flaky pastries still warm from the oven. Even grab-and-go snacks feature unique flavor combinations, adding a touch of luxury to busy days.

The store operates with impressive efficiency: checkout lines move swiftly, self-service kiosks offer flexibility, and staff are knowledgeable yet unobtrusive, always ready to assist without disrupting your pace. More than just a quick pit stop, it’s a testament to the perfect balance of convenience and quality—an ideal choice for urban dwellers who refuse to compromise on taste or efficiency

docs.title: Review of Bayard
docs.text: Google review of Bayard (5 out of 5, by Holly O'Hearn, 5 months ago): I wandered into this little butchery in china town randomly while out adventuring for dumplings and rice rolls. The shop is clean and seems well run compared to other butcher shops nearby. I found it charming that there is almost constantly a woman barking orders in Chinese on a loudspeaker overhead, even though the shop is not that big. Most importantly, at the front of the store they have prepared cantonese lunch/dinner items including these insanely delicious bamboo wrapped sticky rice balls that are all under $4. I got the rice pudding peanut one that had roast pork shoulder and sausage inside… it was unexpectedly good. Apparently there is a nice fish shop next door which i will check out next time. Highly recommend for a quality cantonese snack!

docs.title: Review of Fortune Meat Market
docs.text:
Google review of Fortune Meat Market (1 out of 5, by Mishu Health, 11 months ago): This place used to be great for fresh poultry, but not anymore. I was really disappointed by my recent experience buying chicken feet ，I was charged $5.75 per pound (frozen), while the in-store price for fresh chicken feet was only $1.89.

When I asked around, a friend who shops here often mentioned that some customers  especially non-Chinese speakers ， are sometimes charged higher prices if they don’t question it or mention the local rate. That’s unacceptable.

Also, be cautious if you notice there’s no price tag ， it feels like they decide the price based on who you are. The frozen chicken feet looked old, with freezer burn and lots of ice, which you end up paying for by weight.

It’s really disappointing to see a once-trusted store lose its integrity. I hope management takes this seriously and ensures fair, transparent pricing for everyone. Respect and honesty are what keep loyal customers coming back.

docs.text:
Google review of Prestige Market (5 out of 5, by Joseph Park, a year ago): I recently discovered a fantastic deli that has quickly become my go-to spot for a satisfying meal at any hour. This 24-hour deli offers an impressive variety of sandwiches, each crafted with fresh ingredients and bursting with flavor. Whether you're craving a classic turkey and Swiss or something more adventurous like a famous Chopped Cheese. There's something to satisfy every palate.
What truly sets this deli apart is their exceptional customer service. The staff is consistently friendly and attentive, making you feel welcome no matter what time you walk in. They go above and beyond to ensure you have a pleasant experience, from helping you choose the perfect sandwich to customizing your order to your liking.
In addition to their outstanding sandwiches, the deli also boasts an enticing selection of snacks. Whether you're in the mood for a crunchy bag of chips or a sweet dessert to finish off your meal, you'll find plenty of options to complement your sandwich.
Overall, this deli is a hidden gem that delivers on quality, service, and convenience. It's a must-visit spot for anyone looking for a delicious meal at any hour of the day or night. Highly recommended!

Google review of 7-Eleven (1 out of 5, by Rishita Mehta, a year ago): Absolutely unacceptable customer service. I visited this 7-Eleven and purchased a pack of AA batteries, only to realize minutes later that I actually needed AAA. I returned within five minutes, with the receipt in hand and the product completely unopened.

Despite this, the staff refused to exchange the batteries, claiming that “no exchange on electronic cigarettes” also applied to batteries — which is nowhere stated or implied. That’s not only misleading, it’s borderline gaslighting.

Trying to pass off “electronics” as part of a “no exchange on electronic cigarettes” policy is absurd. If you’re going to deny returns, have the decency to post it clearly and be honest with customers instead of making up rules on the spot.

I won’t be returning to this location, and I’d strongly advise others to check everything carefully — and not expect fairness or accountability if you need help.

Google review of Duane Reade (5 out of 5, by F F, 5 months ago): I have been to many Duane Reades/Walgreens locations across this great nation. This one’s satisfactorily stocked and does a fine job with my prescriptions. But more importantly:

I have seen tired cashiers, indifferent cashiers, cashiers who looked right through me, throughout my life. And then I met Nigel.

Nigel doesn't just work at this Walgreens . He *is* this Walgreens. The man is one of the most amicable people I have ever encountered behind a retail counter. One time when I really needed headphones, he actually hunted them down digging through everything back behind the counter until he found exactly what I needed. That kind of effort is rare. That kind of effort is Nigel.

But here's the kicker. In 23 years of checking out at retailers, I have never signed up for a loyalty card when prompted at the register. It always felt like a trap. A hustle. Which is why I’d always say no.

Nigel asked me once. With a smile. And then proceeded to make the single most compelling case for a loyalty card I have ever heard in my life. I don’t even fully remember what he said. I just know that by the end of it I was nodding, gave him my phone number, my zip code, and frankly would have handed him the keys to my apartment if he'd asked.

Walgreens corporate, if you are reading this: promote this man. Make him regional manager. Make him VP of Customer Experience. Make him CEO. Make him whatever you need to make him because whatever Nigel is doing, it is the entire point of retail. He is the reason the loyalty program exists. He is the reason this location gets five stars.

docs.title: Review of Mei Lai Wah
docs.text:
Google review of Mei Lai Wah (3 out of 5, by Kelly K, a month ago): The pineapple bun with roast pork was tasty. The pork is cubed inside. I also got the regular baked bun with roasted pork. The pineapple gives it an added layer of flavor.

You cannot beat the prices. Under 4$ for the buns and they are a good size.

They take credit cards now, which is a nice update. There’s a kiosk inside where you can order with a card, and it’s actually much quicker. You do have to pay a 3% service charge, but for me, the time saved was worth it.

he line outside is still the same, but once you get inside it splits depending on whether you’re ordering at the counter or kiosk. The line moves pretty quickly in my experience, so don’t let the crowd outside scare you off.

Great value, generous portions, and a tasty little grab-and-go option. I’d come back bc I want to try the baked pineapple
Bun with butter !!

docs.title: Review of Mei Lai Wah
docs.text: Google review of Mei Lai Wah (5 out of 5, by Sebastian Ortega, 4 months ago): Words cannot describe how good their pineapple buns are. It certainly lived up the hype and probably exceeded it. They are so affordable and delicious, it’s dangerous I live this close to this place. The roast pork inside is so unique and savory too. Thankfully, there wasn’t a huge line at 4pm. I would come back every day if I had the patience to wait on line.

docs.title: Review of Mei Lai Wah
docs.text:
Google review of Mei Lai Wah (4 out of 5, by T B, 3 months ago): 4 stars for 4 reasons

1. Pineapple pork bun so good and delicious! Savory, sweet and rich! Must try! Crunchy outside and inside soft so good!

Non pineapple pork bun tasty as well.

Chicken bun was also really good as well! Flavorful and the texture was perfect!

Shrimp dumpling was good as well! Flavorful and perfect cooked!

Shrimp rice roll was good and similar flavor profile as shrimp dumplings

2. Good portion size for the price point

3. Price is great!

4. Food came out relatively quick considering how busy it was

Minus 1 star for 1 reason

1. Soup dumpling was bland and the noodles were clumped together.

Other thing I was ding no indoor seatings or stand up area!

docs.title: Review of Mei Lai Wah
docs.text: Google review of Mei Lai Wah (3 out of 5, by Sam Zhang, a month ago): The service here was quick, I got my food right away despite all the line that forms here all the time, but the food was not as good as what people promoted. I feel like my expectations were too high since everytime I come to Chinatown there are always a line for these buns. But the bun didn't taste out of the world, it was pretty ordinary, it wasn't great but it wasn't bad. The pork meat was very salty and I thought the pineapple part would balance it out but I was wrong, I tasted the texture of the crust but not the flavor. The milk teas here are not fill all the way to the top like other bakeries and milk or creamer was overpowering the tea flavor. Overall, it was an okay yet interesting experience since this is a place I never went to due to all the lines.

docs.title: Review of Mei Lai Wah
docs.text: Google review of Mei Lai Wah (5 out of 5, by Joseph Pratt, 6 months ago): The pineapple buns were literally the best tasting pineapple for I've ever had. I wish I'd bought seven of them. The sesame ball want get warm, I'm not sure if that was intentional or not. It was good just not great because of that. The streamed pork bun on the other hand was great. Chewy, savory. Maybe a tad to sweet but really really good. Would definitely recommend!

docs.title: Review of Liberty Bagels Wall Street
docs.text: Google review of Liberty Bagels Wall Street (5 out of 5, by Niki Pasek, 3 months ago): This place was awesome!  The bagels are so fresh and delicious.  I had the Italian bagel sandwich and my daughter had a chicken avocado.  All the ingredients were very fresh and the service was quick.  Not a lot of room to sit to eat but that is pretty standard I feel in NYC.  It was a great discovery on our day out exploring the city.

docs.title: Review of Liberty Bagels Wall Street
docs.text:
Google review of Liberty Bagels Wall Street (5 out of 5, by Melanie E, 3 months ago): I'm pretty picky about bagels & Liberty makes a delish bagel.

Food: 5/5 they offer a big selection of bagels and the best part is that they make their own cream cheese. If you don't like dairy cream cheese, they make a tofu based cream cheese that is both sweet and savory. They make a big selection of bagels depending on what you want on it. Note: the bagel and filling are a decent portion.

Service: 5/5 you place your order at the back of the store. Service was great.

Atmosphere: 5/5 there's seating available to enjoy your bagel.

docs.title: Review of Liberty Bagels Wall Street
docs.text: Google review of Liberty Bagels Wall Street (5 out of 5, by Dan Bourne, 2 months ago): Looking for your bagel fix? You can’t beat a Liberty Bagel! So many bagel and topping options, there really is something for everyone! We tried ‘The New Yorker’ (egg, brisket, and cheese), ‘The Works’ (egg, sausage, bacon, and hash brown), and ‘The Novie’ (fresh cream cheese, smoked salmon, and avocado). All were delicious and absolutely huge. We had to take some home to eat later!! Definitely recommend!!

docs.title: Review of Liberty Bagels Wall Street
docs.text:
Google review of Liberty Bagels Wall Street (4 out of 5, by CeeCee’s Little Journey, 3 months ago): After taking photos with the Wall Street Bull, we walked a little further and spotted Liberty Bagel, which has been viral online.
Since there was no queue at 5:15 pm, we decided to give it a try.
Perhaps because it was close to closing, they didn’t allow dine‑in at the tables near cashier counter, so we just had a quick bite near the entrance.

We ordered an onion bagel with egg & cheese. The bagel was heated up, with the onion crunch still crispy on the surface.
Everything was served fresh and warm, making the flavor extra satisfying. I don’t regret choosing this combination, though I skipped the rainbow bagel something I now regret a little, as that point of time I thought I will visit again.

Overall, it’s a nice bagel spot. If tourists happen to pass by and see no queue, I’d definitely recommend stopping for a bite. Rating: 4.5/5

docs.title: Review of Liberty Bagels Wall Street
docs.text:
Google review of Liberty Bagels Wall Street (5 out of 5, by Rose Deliu, 6 months ago): Library Bagel absolutely blew me away — this place deserves every bit of a 5-star review.

First off, the chicken tenders… wow. These were hands down the most delicious tenders I’ve ever had. Each piece was thick, juicy, and clearly made with high-quality chicken — not those thin, dry strips you get elsewhere. The breading had the perfect crunch: crispy, golden, and seasoned just right, without overpowering the flavor of the meat. Every bite had that satisfying crunch followed by tender, flavorful chicken that practically melted in your mouth.

And then there’s the rainbow bagel with birthday cake cream cheese — easily one of the most fun and delicious things I’ve eaten in a long time. The bagel itself was soft, fresh, and subtly sweet, but once you add that birthday cake cream cheese, it turns into a full-on flavor explosion. It’s rich, creamy, and packed with that nostalgic cake batter sweetness, with little bursts of flavor in every bite. Somehow it’s indulgent without being overwhelming — just pure happiness in food form.

Between the insanely good chicken tenders and that unforgettable rainbow bagel combo, Library Bagel has completely won me over. I’ll be thinking about this meal for a long time and definitely coming back for more the next time I travel to New York.

A New York City favorite since 1976, this iconic spot delivers rich, creamy cheesecakes with that classic New York-style texture.

We tried three flavors:

Plain Cheesecake — creamy, smooth, perfectly balanced, and not overly sweet. A classic for a reason!

Strawberry Cheesecake — rich and creamy with a sweet strawberry topping that added a bright, fruity twist.

Salted Caramel Cheesecake — decadent, indulgent, and packed with delicious caramel flavor, with just the right touch of salt.

Google review of Ferrara Bakery & Cafe (5 out of 5, by Two Rivers Explorer, 4 months ago): Walking into Ferrara Bakery & Cafe felt like stepping into a classic piece of old New York Italian culture that somehow still survives in the middle of modern Manhattan. The moment you walk through the doors, you’re hit with the smell of espresso, pastries, sugar, fresh cannoli, and that unmistakable old-school bakery atmosphere that immediately makes the place feel warm, alive, and authentic.

What I loved most is that Ferrara doesn’t feel manufactured for tourists — it feels like a place with real history and personality. You can almost imagine generations of Italian New Yorkers stopping in for coffee, pastries, conversations, and family gatherings over the years. There’s a certain energy to the place that feels deeply tied to Little Italy itself.

The dessert selection is honestly overwhelming in the best possible way. Cannoli, tiramisu, cheesecake, cookies, pastries, cakes — every display case feels like a piece of edible art. Everything looked fresh, rich, and made with pride. Sitting there with an espresso and dessert while watching the constant movement of Little Italy outside somehow felt like one of the most New York experiences imaginable.

What really stood out to me was how timeless the place feels. In a city where everything changes constantly, Ferrara still carries that old Italian New York charm — loud conversations, strong coffee, incredible desserts, and people genuinely enjoying themselves. It reminded me that some of the best places in NYC aren’t necessarily the newest or trendiest spots, but the places that have history, character, and soul.

The atmosphere also had that classic Italian New Yorker vibe — welcoming but energetic, traditional but full of personality. You don’t just go there to eat dessert; you go there for the experience, the culture, and the feeling of being connected to a piece of New York history.

Definitely one of my favorite stops in Little Italy, and one of those places that makes you understand why NYC food culture is so legendary.

docs.text: Google review of Leo's Bagels (5 out of 5, by Megan Ferguson, 6 months ago): Today was my first visit to Leo’s Bagels, and everyone was very helpful. I was looking at the menu on the wall and an employee offered me a paper version of the menu so I didn’t have to squint up at the wall to decide what to order. At 12:30pm on Easter Sunday, there was a very short line, and I got in and out pretty quickly (~5-7 min). The employee at the register was very helpful and polite also. I ordered the egg sandwich on an everything bagel toasted with mozzarella cheese, and the melted cheese was very nice. The everything bagel had really good flavor and texture. I also ordered the cinnamon raisin bagel toasted with plain cream cheese, it was delicious. They were very generous with the amount of cream cheese, so I ended up removing some of it. I tried both a savory and a sweet option to get a better idea of their range of options. Both the savory and sweet were good. I’m glad I grabbed extra napkins, because it was a little messy to eat. I spent about $15 total (before tip) for a breakfast sandwich + bagel with cream cheese, which seemed more reasonably priced than other breakfast options in NYC. There’s not much seating in the shop, just a small bartop facing the street (about 8-10 barstools total), so I walked across the street to the Starbucks on Pearl St. and ate at a table inside, which worked well during the heavy rain today (I didn’t want to eat at a park in the rain). Google review of Elbow Bread (5 out of 5, by Ruwan J., 5 months ago): ((4.75 stars))

Elbow Bread is a small bakery planted at the intersection of Ludlow, Division, and Canal Streets. cozy brightly-lit space--no seats inside but there are small tables set up outside for those who want to place to perch, but most customers grab-and-go or grab-and-eat-on-the-go. there are a variety of baked eats here from various sour dough loaves to sweeter options like cookies and kolaches to savory options like bialys and schmaltz scallion knots as well as other comfort eats. if you can stop here in the morning during the week--i would say that is your best bet as items on menu will run out way before closing time which is like 3 pm on weekdays and a little later on weekends. definitely try the pretzels, when you see them as that is one of the signature items, but my current favorite is the everything bialy with cream cheese--a chewy airy bread roll sprinkled with poppy seeds, sesame seeds, dried garlic, dried onion, and salt and a dollop of cream cheese. it's one satisfying comfort food in the bread quality alone but the cream cheese adds that creamy fatty-ness and combined with the "everything flavor" makes for enjoyable bites from beginning to end. nothing against bagels, but you haven't really lived as a New Yorker unless you have eaten a great bialy...and Elbow Bread serves a great one. the coffee is pretty good too--probably a medium roast which pairs with sweet eats as well as savory ones without detracting. service is pleasant and quick but not rushed. while Elbow Bread has its fans from the LES / Dimes Square / Chinatown area, people definitely travel here from all across the city to indulge some finely baked carbs...and it is very much worth the trip.

Google review of Crispy Heaven (5 out of 5, by Brett Ari Fischer, 8 months ago): At Crispy Heaven, the crust alone makes a statement.

Before you even get to the toppings, the pizza comes out with that blistered, lightly charred edge and soft, airy center that tells you it was handled properly. It’s the kind of place where the food lands on the table and everyone instinctively reaches in.

Crispy Heaven leans into comfort food, but it does it with real care. The bread basket had a crisp exterior and a warm, chewy interior that actually tasted like fresh bread, not filler.

I don’t eat pepperoni or cheeseburgers, but my friend ordered both and was genuinely impressed. The pepperoni pie had a balanced sauce-to-cheese ratio with a nice kick from the toppings, and the burger was thick, juicy, and properly cooked with melted cheddar and a pile of crisp fries. Based on how quickly both disappeared, they clearly deliver.

The margherita with fresh basil and burrata in the center was the one I focused on. Once the burrata started to melt into the tomato sauce, it tied everything together in a way that felt rich but not heavy.

The tacos were another standout for me. Well-seasoned meat, fresh cilantro and onion, and a creamy green sauce that added brightness without overpowering the flavor of the beef.

The steak plate was cooked exactly how you want it, with roasted vegetables that still had texture and life to them instead of being overdone.

And the service was excellent. Warm, attentive, and genuinely friendly without hovering. It felt easy and welcoming from start to finish.

Places like Crispy Heaven give a block personality. As someone who’s constantly around the city for real estate, I always pay attention to the restaurants that feel like they actually belong in the neighborhood. This is one of them.

If you’re craving pizza, tacos, burgers, or a solid steak dinner in a relaxed setting, Crispy Heaven lives up to its name.

Google review of Tai Pan Bakery (5 out of 5, by Julian Jung, 7 months ago): Tai Pan Bakery has one of the best egg tarts so far in the city! I love that they have both the flaky and cookie crust egg tarts along with the porteguese egg tart. The flaky crust is perfect, layers flake off as you bite into it and the filling is not too eggy and not too sweet. Their cookie crust egg tart has a satisfying soft snap as you bite into the oval end. I also love that it's oval shaped!! The only other bakery that I know of that does cookie crust oval shaped egg tarts is Saint Anna Bakery in Chicago!! Both egg tarts were a delightful snack! ☺️ The porteguese egg tart filling was super creamy and the richness of the caramelized "brûléed" top was the perfect contrast. Even the crust has slight caramelization on the inner edges.

If you haven’t been, stop by Tai Pan Bakery for their egg tarts - it's a must! While you're there, try their other bakery items as well. There's the classic pineapple bun, cha siu bao (BBQ pork bun), and the ham+egg bun. Plenty of sponge cake desserts too if you have a sweet tooth!!

docs.title: Review of Spongies Cafe
docs.text:
Google review of Spongies Cafe (5 out of 5, by ZiENZiEN Blog, 3 months ago): As someone who absolutely loves bread (I’m Thai, but I could honestly eat bread instead of rice 😆), I have to recommend this place.

If you’re visiting Chinatown, this is definitely a hidden gem worth stopping by. Their sponge cakes are affordable, incredibly soft, light, and never dry.

The staff is also very friendly. They told me their cakes are baked, unlike many other shops that grill theirs, which gives them a really soft and fluffy texture.

I’ve tried several flavors, including Thai tea, coffee, and chocolate, but my absolute favorite is the Pandan Coconut. The pandan aroma is so fragrant, and it contains real shredded coconut, which adds a wonderful texture to every bite.

I originally planned to buy just five cakes, but after chatting with the staff for a while, I somehow walked out with twelve! 😂 I ended up sharing them with several friends, and every single one of them said the same thing: “These are so good!”

You can really feel that this is a family-run business. The atmosphere is warm, welcoming, and genuine, which makes the whole experience even better.

I can’t recommend this place enough. If you’re in Chinatown and love soft, fluffy sponge cakes, don’t miss it—you probably won’t be disappointed.

Google review of Pi Bakerie (5 out of 5, by Carl Reviews, 3 months ago): We visited Pi Bakery on Cedar Street in Manhattan on a cold, snowy day, and it was the perfect cosy escape from the weather. The place was warm and welcoming, and we enjoyed a delicious warm apple pie that was absolutely gorgeous. They even whipped up some cream to go with it.

The staff were exceptionally friendly and helpful. We also had a hot chocolate and an Earl Grey tea, both of which were spot on. It was simply lovely to receive such genuinely excellent service, and we would happily return.

Unfortunately, our return visit in July was disappointing.

The service was noticeably less friendly, and the prices now seem extremely high. We ordered the apple pie they are known for and asked whether we could have cream or ice cream on the side, but neither was available. Instead, we were offered a single scoop of Greek yoghurt, which was charged at $4 per person. That felt excessive for what was provided.

The food is still good, but the overall pricing is becoming very difficult to justify, particularly when the service no longer feels as welcoming as it did before.

docs.title: Review of Bubby's
docs.text:
Google review of Bubby's (3 out of 5, by Myriam Ward, 3 months ago): We had heard a lot about Bubby’s pancakes, so after trying the ones at Golden Diner, we had to check them out. They’re good, but nowhere near the best in the city.

We ordered the pancake flight, which includes three James Beard pancakes: caramelized banana with toasted walnuts, blueberry, and Nutella with macerated strawberries and whipped cream.

The pancakes themselves are quite good—fluffy and light. However, they didn’t taste as freshly made to order as the ones at Golden Diner, possibly because this is a much larger restaurant. But then again, they weren’t on the same level as Golden Diner in terms of fluffiness.

As for the toppings, they were good but not very generous. The whipped cream was fine, but nothing particularly memorable. The pancakes didn’t really absorb the toppings.

If you can get a reservation, it’s worth trying, but personally, I would still prefer to wait in line for Golden Diner. Overall, we were slightly disappointed with the experience.

docs.title: Review of Bubby's
docs.text:
Google review of Bubby's (3 out of 5, by Niran Zikman, 2 months ago): A bit overrated in my opinion. The food is tasty, the portions are generous, and you'll definitely leave full, but there's nothing particularly memorable or unique about it.

One thing that stood out was how quickly the food arrived. It was almost suspiciously fast, which makes me think much of it is prepared in advance due to the restaurant's popularity. That said, everything came out hot and tasted fresh, so I can't really complain about that.

The biggest downside was the service. The staff came across as cold and somewhat condescending, and it often felt like we were bothering them whenever we needed something.

To make matters worse, getting the check took an unreasonably long time. We waited, tried to get someone's attention multiple times, and were simply ignored. Eventually, we got up and walked to the register to pay because we just wanted to leave.

Overall, the food is good, but the service made the experience much less enjoyable, and I don't think it lives up to the hype.

docs.title: Review of Bubby's
docs.text:
Google review of Bubby's (4 out of 5, by Doah Kwon, 3 months ago): The salad was surprisingly good (just as good as what you’d get at a dedicated salad spot). The turkey sandwich was also good, and I liked that it had onions inside. The staff was super friendly and made us feel really welcome!

The peanut butter pie was good. As a huge peanut butter lover, it basically tasted like pure peanut butter in a good way. The pancakes were soft, fluffy, and exactly what you want from a classic pancake. The portions were huge tho! The two of us ordered a sandwich, a salad, and one pancake to share, and we still couldn’t finish the pancake. We added chocolate chips and whipped cream, and adding the chocolate chips was definitely the right call.

My favorite pancake flavor was the Nutella, while my friend’s favorite was the banana. We went on Saturday, July 4th and the wait was about 30 minutes, which wasn’t bad considering the holiday. My only wish is that they had an Americano instead of just cold brew!

Their fried chicken is some of the best I’ve had. The pancakes are always fluffy and very filling. I prefer the sourdough pancakes only because they’re thinner and not as heavy. They have great fresh oj as well. The vibe inside is always fun and good energy in the mornings.

docs.title: Review of Golden Diner
docs.text:
Google review of Golden Diner (5 out of 5, by Myriam Ward, 3 months ago): A must-visit restaurant in New York.

The rave reviews of Golden Diner are absolutely deserved. You often hear it’s the place to find the best pancakes in the city—and it’s true. They are light, fluffy, and incredibly flavorful, with syrup and a hint of lemon zest that make every bite a delight.

We also tried the Korean fried chicken wings and loved them. They were perfectly crispy, with a well-balanced crust and a sweet and spicy glaze—truly delicious.

Finally, we ordered the Chicken Katsu Club, and once again, Golden Diner delivered. Every bite was satisfying: the chicken was perfectly fried, and the red cabbage added a fresh, crunchy contrast.

Would we order the same dishes again? Absolutely. In fact, we’re already looking forward to coming back soon—this meal was that memorable.

One small note: you may want to ask the staff not to bring all the dishes at once, as they can cool down while you’re enjoying them one at a time.

Without a doubt, Golden Diner is worth a visit—you won’t be disappointed and will leave with an unforgettable dining experience.
.

docs.text: Google review of Golden Diner (5 out of 5, by Jennifer Serrano, 3 months ago): Great little spot! My hubby wanted to check it out from seeing it on social media a few times so we decided to visit while on a trip. I got the honey butter pancakes (double) and my hubby got the wings. The food was pretty good! The pancakes were super fluffy, reminded me of like jiffy batter maybe and had a lemon garnish, a nice touch! They were very satisfying I could say! The waitlist was pretty long, so best to reserve ahead of time if they let you. We waited an hour n a half so we’re like, it’s gotta be good and worth the wait! We did get a counter/bar seat which was kind of cool because I got to watch a lot of the kitchen staff make some cool stuff like sandwiches like the chicken katsu club. One thing I can say, though is the actual server never really made an attempt to talk to us or see how we were doing if we needed anything which we did sometimes so I do kind of wish the service was better, the girl out front taking reservations was kind though I can say. I know it’s a busy city and I’m on vacation from Florida so I’m just probably being picky but overall was pretty good. The prices were really good in my opinion and you really do get pretty big portions. They also had outdoor seating we believe but we had been running so we just wanted to get inside to some AC but glad we stopped in.

Google review of Thai Diner (5 out of 5, by 3dogs1monkey, 4 months ago): While visiting NY, our daughter wanted to have lunch with our niece at a Thai restaurant, I and my wife just followed. Google review of Thai Diner (4 out of 5, by Doah Kwon, 3 months ago): We came here for lunch and two of us got the lobster noodles, french toast, chicken liver, and morning glory. The morning glory was super flavorful, and the chicken liver was really good with the peanuts and savory seasoning.

My favorite was definitely the French toast. I thought the dark filling inside was chocolate at first, but it turned out to be condensed brown sugar. It was sooo good! The toast had a great texture, and the Thai butter on the side made it even better. The lobster noodles was not that good tho. They weren’t bad but they were probably our least favorite dish and nothing really stood out about them. And the staff was super friendly and so welcoming!

docs.title: Review of Thai Diner
docs.text:
Google review of Thai Diner (5 out of 5, by Nicole C, 4 months ago): If you ever loved Uncle Boons, Thai Diner will definitely feel familiar—but it doesn’t quite hit the same highs. Service was fast and attentive, which set a great tone, but the food ended up being pretty hit or miss. The som tum salad was a standout and easily one of the best things on the menu—bright, balanced, and genuinely exciting. The crab fried rice had excellent texture and plenty of fresh crab, but the flavor just didn’t have that same depth Boons used to deliver.

The mussels and fries were a mixed bag: fries were perfectly seasoned and crisp, and the mussels were clean, but the sauce felt one-note and the sweet pickled onions threw the whole dish off. The fried snapper was cooked well but leaned overly sweet—I’d definitely order the sauce on the side next time so it doesn’t overpower everything. The accompanying rice was a miss: under-seasoned, mushy, and mixed with large pieces of herbs and cucumbers that didn’t quite work due to the texture of the rice. The spicy tamarind margarita also skewed too sweet.

That said, the coconut sundae was incredible and honestly worth coming back for on its own. Overall, I’d come back for the nostalgia (and dessert).

docs.title: Review of Thai Diner
docs.text:
Google review of Thai Diner (5 out of 5, by Mayeku Aggrey, 4 months ago): I ended up at Thai Diner after wandering around Nolita for a while and looking for somewhere that felt casual but memorable. The place was busy without feeling chaotic, and once the food started arriving I understood why people keep coming back. I started with the khao soi, which came out steaming hot with a rich curry broth and noodles that somehow stayed perfectly textured all the way through the meal. It was comforting without feeling heavy.

I also ordered the Thai disco fries because they sounded too interesting to pass up. They were crispy underneath and covered with a flavorful curry sauce that made them disappear much faster than expected. The chicken satay had a nice char from the grill and paired well with the peanut sauce, while the roti was soft and perfect for scooping up every bit of curry left on the plate.

What I liked most was that nothing felt overly complicated. The flavors were bold but approachable, and every dish felt like something you would happily order again. By the end of the meal I was already looking around at other tables wondering what I should try next time.

docs.title: Review of Au Cheval
docs.text:
Google review of Au Cheval (5 out of 5, by Carolyn T, a month ago): My fiancé and I experienced true “unreasonable hospitality” from Lucas, making our dinner unforgettable. His kindness, attention to detail, and ability to anticipate our needs showed us just how far he was willing to go to make our evening special.

Each dish was beautifully and artfully composed. Since it was our first visit, we ordered several rich dishes back-to-back. Everything was delicious, but next time, I would create a little more balance.

The kale Caesar dressing was bright, acidic, and addictive, while the wings had incredible crunch and flavor. Of course, the burger was the star of the show. It is fully loaded, wildly popular for good reason, and a lot of food if you order it with all the fixings, so beware! The French dip was also delicious, especially with the au jus and horseradish sauce. The mac and cheese was a little too heavy for my taste, though still undeniably delicious.

Lastly, dessert was so memorable. I loved the contrast of the refreshing strawberry gelato with the warm hot fudge. The chocolate cream pie was decadent and incredible, with the fluffiest whipped cream.

***Half portions of the wings and salad are available, which is perfect if you want to try more of the menu.

docs.text: Google review of Eataly (4 out of 5, by Layna Perry, 3 months ago): This is for the Eataly on Liberty. This place is always packed. The food is always good. It’s great for a large group, you don’t feel claustrophobic like some places in Manhattan. We had seven for dinner tonight. I unfortunately did not take photos of the appetizers, or the meal. We did the meatballs, broccolini, calamari; a few glasses of red wine; a salmon, a few steaks, bunch of pastas, and a chicken Milanese. Everyone enjoyed their food. They’re doing something different with the tiramisu since the last time I was there. There are lady fingers in it now, and it’s a bit celebratory how they unwrap it. We also tried the panna cotta, the Amalfi, and limoncello. My only knock was that it might be the dirtiest bathroom I’ve ever used in a restaurant. The bins in each stall were overflowing. I’m going to leave out some details, but it was unpleasant. The labyrinth of the marketplace is such a great vibe. And the location is a huge thumbs up.

Another so so restaurant but not in a so so place.

Google review of Joe’s Pizza (4 out of 5, by CeeCee’s Little Journey, 3 months ago): Even though I was already full, I couldn’t skip Joe’s Pizza, one of the city’s famous spots. I decided to order just one slice to try. The staff recommended the classic cheese flavor, so I went with that.

The slice was quite nice actually, with thin crust, simple, and satisfying.
It’s the kind of classic pizza that never goes wrong.
On the table, they had cheese, chili flakes, and garlic powder for extra flavor, which making thoughtful for customer to add on based on preference.

The store was crowded, but the turnover was fast, making it a good place for a quick bite.
Overall, a solid experience and I’m giving 4.2/5.

docs.title: Review of Joe’s Pizza
docs.text: Google review of Joe’s Pizza (5 out of 5, by Suhrob Nuriddinov, 3 months ago): Joe’s Pizza on Fulton Street is exactly what New York pizza should be. Thin, crispy crust, perfectly balanced sauce, and that classic mozzarella stretch that makes every bite satisfying. I stopped in for a quick slice and ended up wishing I had ordered more. The pizza was served fresh, hot, and packed with flavor. The crust had just the right amount of crunch while still being soft and foldable -the true New York way. The ingredients tasted fresh, and you can tell why Joe’s has earned such a strong reputation over the years. The staff was friendly, the service was quick, and the atmosphere had that authentic no-frills NYC pizza vibe that both locals and visitors appreciate. If you’re anywhere near the Financial District and craving real New York pizza, Joe’s Pizza is absolutely worth the stop. One of the best slices in Manhattan, hands down. Highly recommended!

docs.title: Review of Fraunces Tavern
docs.text:
Google review of Fraunces Tavern (2 out of 5, by Kenya, 2 months ago): (Long review) I recently visited Fraunces Tavern, and the building itself is absolutely beautiful. It’s full of history and has a fascinating story behind it, which made the experience unique. A big part of my visit was to celebrate my husband’s birthday.

Unfortunately, the food did not meet my expectations, especially considering the prices. The dishes looked delicious when they arrived, but the food was literally as cold as the dining area. The flavor was lacking, and the temperature was a major disappointment. We ordered the mac and cheese, and the cheese wasn’t even melted, it was literally sitting on top of the dish.

The service was okay. Our waitress seemed busy, but the restaurant and museum are located in a very busy area and appear to have a steady flow of customers, so that was understandable.

We did finish our meals and didn’t complain at the time because we didn’t want to make an issue of it. The portions were generous, which was a positive. Overall, I’m glad I got to experience the historic atmosphere and see the restaurant/museum, but I wouldn’t return for the food. It’s definitely worth visiting for the history and the visuals, but my dining experience was disappointing.

docs.title: Review of Fraunces Tavern
docs.text:
Google review of Fraunces Tavern (5 out of 5, by David Green, 2 months ago): If you are looking for an unforgettable night out in New York City that perfectly blends deep American roots with an incredible contemporary vibe, look no further than the historic Fraunces Tavern on a Saturday night.

Stepping into this legendary establishment feels like taking a direct journey back to the late 1700s, but the energy inside is entirely vibrant, welcoming, and alive. We visited this past weekend and wound up celebrating a birthday with a group of three incredible women, and to lean fully into the atmosphere of the venue, they donned colonial-style wigs to look exactly like the founding fathers. It was an absolute hit. Please see pic!

The atmospheric, historic charm of the building paired beautifully with our playful tribute to George Washington’s old stomping grounds.The highlight of the evening was undoubtedly the live music. From 8:00 PM to 11:00 PM, the immensely talented Hannah Ray Teal, in a duo with her talented guitarist Will, took the stage, delivering a captivating performance. Her soulful vocals and fantastic guitar playing filled the room, providing the perfect soundtrack for an exceptional night.

Matching the stellar entertainment was the top-tier hospitality. The staff members were incredibly friendly, fast, and attentive, providing professional service throughout the entire evening. The crowd itself added another wonderful layer to the experience; the tavern attracts a fascinating, diverse mix of international patrons, making for great conversations and a global, upscale energy. Fraunces Tavern delivers on every front—history, exceptional live music, and a crowd that knows how to have a great time. It is the ultimate spot for a legendary NYC night out.

Google review of Manhatta (5 out of 5, by Alaleh - FoodyTO, 4 months ago): We visited Manhatta on a Saturday for my birthday and had a wonderful experience. The restaurant is located on the 60th floor of 28 Liberty Street and offers breathtaking views of Lower Manhattan, the Statue of Liberty, Staten Island, and New York Harbor.

Before our table was ready, we waited in the lounge area and enjoyed the incredible views. A thoughtful touch was the personalized birthday note waiting on our table when we arrived, which made the occasion feel extra special.

The atmosphere was elegant but welcoming, and it was interesting to see that many other guests were also celebrating birthdays and special occasions there.

We came for lunch and ordered the two-course lunch menu. To start, we had the “Beef Tartare” and “Fluke Crudo”, followed by the “Grilled Sea Bass”, “Dry-Aged Burger”, and “Lobster Ravioli” for our mains. For dessert, we enjoyed the “Coconut Mousse” and paired the meal with red wine and the “Land of the Sun” cocktail. The restaurant has an excellent selection of red, white, and sparkling wines.

The service was friendly and attentive without ever making us feel rushed.. We took our time, enjoyed the food, the drinks, and the stunning views, making it a memorable birthday celebration.

docs.title: Review of Manhatta
docs.text:
Google review of Manhatta (5 out of 5, by Linh, 4 months ago): Manhatta has officially become one of my favorite restaurants of all time.

The experience starts with the stunning views from the 60th floor overlooking New York City, but the food and service are what truly make this place special. Every member of the staff was warm, knowledgeable, and attentive without ever being overbearing.

We ordered the four-course menu and every course was outstanding. For the first course, we had the Jonah Crab with asparagus, apple, and sorrel, along with the Bluefin Tuna with jicama, shiso, and white soy vinaigrette. The crab was honestly the best crab dish I’ve ever eaten—sweet, delicate, and perfectly balanced. The tuna was equally impressive, incredibly fresh and beautifully prepared.

For the second course, we chose the Seared Scallop with nduja, watermelon radish, and pea shoots, as well as the Glazed Sweetbreads with morel mushrooms, arugula pesto, and horseradish. Both dishes were expertly executed and packed with flavor.

For our mains, we had the Butter Poached Lobster and the Lamb Loin & Rib. The lobster was excellent, but the real surprise was the Koshihikari rice—it was absolutely amazing and one of the most memorable components of the entire meal. The lamb was perfectly cooked and paired wonderfully with the fava bean pesto, almond, and pecorino.

Dessert was the Pistachio Cake with strawberry and crème fraîche chamomile ice cream, which was a fantastic ending to the meal.

We also enjoyed several mezcal cocktails and wine pairings throughout dinner, all of which complemented the food beautifully.

Between the breathtaking views, exceptional service, creative menu, and unforgettable dishes, Manhatta delivered one of the best dining experiences I’ve had in NYC. Highly recommended, and I can’t wait to come back.

docs.title: Review of Shu Jiao Fu Zhou
docs.text:
Google review of Shu Jiao Fu Zhou (5 out of 5, by Bran, 6 months ago): ⭐⭐⭐⭐⭐

If you are walking through Chinatown and want a true, authentic New York food experience, this place is an absolute MUST. Shu Jiao Fu Zhou is the definition of “don’t judge a book by its cover.” It’s small, no-frills, and always packed—but that’s exactly how you know it’s the real deal.

The dumplings here are hands down some of the best you’ll ever have—perfectly thin skins, juicy, flavorful filling, and made fresh. You can taste the authenticity in every bite. And the peanut noodles? Unreal. Rich, savory, and incredibly satisfying—simple but packed with flavor.

What makes this spot even more incredible is the value. You can walk in hungry and walk out completely full for just a few dollars. It’s one of those rare places in NYC where the quality is top-tier and the prices are still unbelievably low.

The vibe is classic Chinatown—busy, fast-paced, and full of energy. You might have to wait or grab a quick seat, but that’s all part of the experience. This is real NYC street food culture at its finest.

Bottom line:
Cheap, authentic, and insanely delicious. This is the kind of spot locals try to keep a secret—but once you go, you’ll be telling everyone about it.

A true 5-star Chinatown staple.

Google review of Kiki's (4 out of 5, by Crazy Sandwich, 7 months ago): We had a delightful casual experience at this restaurant, where the food was absolutely delicious! We indulged in the dips, mixed grill, calamari, and spanakopita, and each dish was a treat for the taste buds. Even the dessert was a sweet ending to our meal. The ambiance was warm and cozy, making it a perfect spot for a relaxed dining experience.

However, we did have a minor issue with the service. It seemed like our table was a bit overlooked at times. docs.title: Review of Kiki's
docs.text:
Google review of Kiki's (5 out of 5, by Brooklyn Roach, 8 months ago): Finally made it to Kiki’s and I’m happy to say it was worth all the hype. They don’t take reservations for small groups though so there’s often a wait, but we went at an odd time on Valentine’s Day and were able to be seated quickly.

Service was great and the restaurant had a really cozy feel that definitely matched the vibe of enjoying coastal Greek food. The calamari was some of the best I’ve ever had, super fresh with a perfect crumb and the right amount of crisp. The other appetizer we got was the grilled loukaniko, which is like an orange sausage. I definitely think these two were the standouts of our experience and I’d come back for the appetizers alone.

I ordered the Branzino and it was also very fresh with a nice crispy skin, very bony but that’s to be expected. They also came with lemon potatoes that were nicely drenched in a lemony butter sauce. My boyfriend ordered the kebabs, which was a special not featured on the menu— they were full of flavor and very delicious.

Kiki’s also had lots of small touches I personally really enjoyed that made it feel very cozy and welcoming, like small coat hooks behind the tables and lots of authentic Greek touches. I also didn’t feel like they rushed us at any point, despite being very busy and I appreciated that.

Overall I thought the prices were good too for the quality of the food, definitely try and come on an off day or time though because I’ve tried to get in before and the wait times were ridiculous. I’d recommend Kiki’s for a date night and some authentic Greek food.

Google review of Ceres (5 out of 5, by Eric Helferich, 3 months ago): Two former Eleven Madison Park chefs decided to open a pizza joint, so you already know your boy had to pull up.
​There are no walk-up slices here—whole pies only. It was packed, so I had to use maximum tactical efficiency. I spotted a few women waiting in line, executed a flawless negotiation, and convinced them to team up on a two-pie operation: one classic Cheese, one Nduja. We secured the goods, split the assets, and I went on my way.
​First up: The Cheese Pie (San Marzano tomatoes, scamorza, mozzarella, premium olive oil). Cracker-crisp crust, zero flop, absolute perfection. 100% worth the hype.
​Next: The Nduja Pie. Spicy Calabrian pork sausage, creamy fresh burrata, and a drizzle of 9-year aged balsamic. Bro. Unbelievable. Easily one of the best slices in NYC.
​If you find yourself in New York, you don't just eat pizza—you make executive moves for it. Ceres is an absolute must-stop. 🍕🔥

docs.title: Review of Cecconi's DUMBO
docs.text:
Google review of Cecconi's DUMBO (4 out of 5, by Ashley Perez, a month ago): Cecconi’s Dumbo definitely delivers when it comes to the views and atmosphere. The location is beautiful and the ambiance makes it a great spot for a nice lunch or dinner. It can get very busy on nice days, and parking in the area can be difficult, but that’s pretty much expected in Dumbo.

The food was delicious and the customer service was great—no complaints there at all. My only reason for giving 4 stars instead of 5 is that I wish they had more meat options. There was only one steak option when we visited, and it was a steak for two for around $190. I would have loved to see a good steak option for one person on the menu.

For an idea of pricing, we had 1 appetizer, 2 entrées, 2 drinks, 2 coffees, and 2 desserts, and the total came to around $270 before tip.

Overall, a great experience with amazing views, delicious food, and excellent service. Add a steak option for one and this would easily be a 5-star experience for me.
