docs.title: Review of Cecconi's DUMBO
docs.text:
Google review of Cecconi's DUMBO (4 out of 5, by Joe Stark, 4 months ago): I recently had dinner at Cecconi’s DUMBO, located at 55 Water Street in Brooklyn, NY, and overall it was a fantastic experience. From the moment I walked in, I was impressed by the atmosphere. The restaurant has a sophisticated yet welcoming vibe, with elegant décor, warm lighting, and a stylish interior that perfectly complements its iconic DUMBO location. It feels upscale without being intimidating, making it a great place for date nights, family gatherings, or dinner with friends.

The food was excellent from start to finish. We started with appetizers and fresh bread, which set the tone for a memorable meal. The pizza was one of the highlights of the evening. It had a perfectly blistered crust, fresh ingredients, and a wonderful balance of flavors. You can tell the pizza is made with care and attention to quality.

I also ordered the steak, and it was outstanding. It was cooked exactly as requested, tender, juicy, and full of flavor. Every bite was satisfying, and the quality of the ingredients really stood out. The portions were generous, and the presentation was beautiful. Everything we ordered felt thoughtfully prepared and worthy of the restaurant’s reputation.

Another aspect that made the experience enjoyable was the service. Our server was friendly, professional, attentive, and knowledgeable about the menu. The staff checked on us regularly and ensured that everything was running smoothly throughout the meal. Great service can elevate a dining experience, and the team at Cecconi’s certainly delivered.

The only downside of an otherwise excellent visit was the payment process. It appears the restaurant is still using an older POS system that does not efficiently handle split checks. Since our group wanted to split the bill, the server had to manually calculate each person’s share using a calculator. While the staff handled it professionally, the process took longer than expected and felt outdated compared to modern restaurant payment systems that can split bills instantly. Upgrading the POS system would greatly improve convenience for both customers and staff.

Despite that minor issue, Cecconi’s DUMBO remains a restaurant I would highly recommend. The beautiful ambiance, delicious pizza, perfectly cooked steak, and exceptional service made for a memorable dining experience. I look forward to returning and enjoying another meal at this wonderful Brooklyn destination.

docs.text: Google review of House of Joy (4 out of 5, by Daniel Ng, 7 months ago): My favorite dim sum spot in the U.S. so far. I haven’t found any place in DC that serves dim sum the traditional way, directly from trolley carts like in Hong Kong. This restaurant stays busy all day, so sharing a table with other diners is almost guaranteed. You simply order dishes straight from the carts as they pass by, and the staff stamps each item on your order sheet. When you’re done, you take the sheet to the counter to pay. It feels very authentic, just like the Hong Kong experience. And the best part? The prices are very reasonable, especially for New York City.

docs.text:
Google review of LOS TACOS No.1 (3 out of 5, by Maha, 3 months ago): ⭐⭐⭐☆☆

I visited this place because of its high Google ratings, but unfortunately, the experience did not fully meet my expectations.

• Food: We tried the tacos, and they were much spicier than expected. Everyone in our group found them quite hot, so we didn’t try the salsa since the tacos already had plenty of heat. The flavors were interesting, but the spice level made it harder to fully enjoy the other flavors.

• Vegetarian Options: The only vegetarian option available was the Nopal (grilled cactus) taco. It was nice to have a vegetarian choice, but adding more vegetarian options would make the menu more appealing to a wider range of customers.

• Service: The staff was friendly and welcoming. Most of the team spoke Spanish, and they were helpful and kind throughout our visit.

• Seating: The place has standing tables, but no traditional seating. Personally, I think I would have enjoyed the experience more if there were seats where we could sit and enjoy the tacos.

• Overall Experience: I’m glad we tried it once, but the experience did not match the expectations created by the high Google ratings. It was still a good experience to try, especially for those who enjoy spicy tacos, but I was hoping for a more balanced flavor experience and a more comfortable dining setup.

Google review of LOS TACOS No.1 (5 out of 5, by Plate Cleaner Club, 4 months ago): 🌮🔥 If you're near the World Trade Center and need a quick bite, I can see why there's always a line at Los Tacos No. 1!

I stopped by and ordered the steak quesadilla, chicken tacos, Jamaica juice, and the cactus salad. The standout for me was definitely the steak quesadilla 🤤. The steak was incredibly tender, the cheese was perfectly melted, and every bite was packed with flavor.

The chicken tacos were also excellent, served on fresh tortillas with simple toppings that let the ingredients shine 🌮. I paired everything with a Jamaica juice, which was refreshing and slightly sweet, and of course a Coca-Cola.

I was also curious about the cactus salad since it was my first time trying cactus. Honestly, it tasted pretty similar to peppers and added a nice fresh veggie component to the meal 🥗.

Despite the constant crowd, the staff kept the line moving quickly, and my food came out fast. If you're looking for a delicious, affordable, and quick meal in Lower Manhattan, this spot is absolutely worth the stop. I'll definitely be back! 🌟🌮🔥

docs.text:
Google review of Joe's Shanghai (5 out of 5, by Monica Ro, 3 months ago): ★★★★★

Joe’s Shanghai absolutely lived up to the hype. If you’re in Chinatown, this place is a must.

Of course we had to order the famous soup dumplings, and they were every bit as good as everyone says. The wrappers were perfectly thin, packed with rich, flavorful broth, and the pork filling was delicious. Just be careful they come out piping hot!

We also shared the chicken fried rice and General Tso’s chicken. Both portions were generous, fresh, and full of flavor. The General Tso’s had the perfect balance of crispy chicken and a sweet, savory sauce, and I loved that it came with fresh broccoli on the side.

The restaurant has a lively, bustling atmosphere that feels like a true New York Chinatown experience. Service was quick despite how busy they were, and our food arrived hot and fresh.

If you’re visiting NYC and want authentic Shanghainese cuisine, Joe’s Shanghai deserves a spot on your list. Great food, generous portions, and those soup dumplings alone are worth the visit. I’d definitely come back.

docs.title: Review of Joe's Shanghai
docs.text:
Google review of Joe's Shanghai (5 out of 5, by Letiicia Georgieva, 3 months ago): Walking in, I already had a feeling this was going to be one of those places where you forget about checking your phone because the food keeps showing up and grabbing your attention. The dining room had a busy energy but never felt overwhelming. Once everything landed on the table, we ended up reaching for the soup dumplings first, then somehow kept rotating between the scallion pancakes, crispy shredded beef, and shrimp fried rice without really deciding what to eat next.

The soup dumplings absolutely lived up to what I hoped for. They were packed with hot broth and the wrapper held together just enough if you took your time. The crispy shredded beef had that sweet and crunchy coating that made it easy to keep picking at even after I felt full. Between bites, the scallion pancakes added something simple but satisfying, especially dipped into the sauce left from the dumplings.

By the end of the meal the table looked like we had ordered too much, but somehow very little was left. It felt like the kind of restaurant that's easy to recommend because the food is comforting without trying too hard. I'd happily come back the next time I'm in Chinatown just to order the same combination again.

docs.title: Review of Wah Fung No.1 Fast Food
docs.text:
Google review of Wah Fung No.1 Fast Food (5 out of 5, by MSJ, a month ago): A long wait for the food, especially on the weekend. But cant beat the price, roast pork and duck over rice for $9.00. Food was great, the portion was good, and there are size options from small $6 ~ large $9.50 choice of meat from pork, duck, and chicken over rice. The rice goes under, then sautéed cabbages, meat gets chopped and placed on top and the broth gets poured over so no extra sauces or seasonings required.
Even thought it was busy and lines were never ending, the employee was very nice and quick. They do sell sodas on the side, just grab them from the fridge after you order. I would recommend this location if you have time to wait around, its good weather, and you want to experience the authentic New York Chinese takeout. But it can be a long wait, the end of the line for me was at the end of the block and time was Saturday 4pm. Personally I like the pork better than the duck.

No Atmospheres. Walk in, order, grab your food and walk out. Very limited space inside, for maybe 4-5 people at most.

docs.title: Review of Wah Fung No.1 Fast Food
docs.text:
Google review of Wah Fung No.1 Fast Food (4 out of 5, by Myriam Ward, 3 months ago): We tried 4 of the top rated spots in Chinatown to get char siu over rice. Here is our ranking:

1) New Kim Tuong
2) Wah Fung Number 1
3) Hay Hay Roasted
4) Tin Wong

Very good roast pork on rice for an unbeatable price. Probably the best value meal in Manhattan.

No cash, hole in the wall type of place, Wah Fung serves roast duck, chicken, pork and crispy pig over rice. The line may look long but it moves fast, and the entire establishment is operated by only 2 men inside which is extremely expensive.

I ordered the large roast pork on rice for $8.5. As you can see in the photo, it’s a really generous portions where they definitely do not skimp on the meat.

The roast pork itself has the perfect amount of sweetness. The texture is exactly as you would not expect for Cantonese roast pork - a satisfying hearty, meaty consistency. The roast pork sits on top of a bed of white rice and steamed cabbage. I was very pleasantly surprised by the rice - it was moist and flavourful due to the sauce that the chef poured over the rice and vegetables before adding the meat.

My only criticisms would be that the slices were a tiny bit too thin for my liking, and maybe the sauce could have a stronger umami flavour, but giving the incredible price, I really can’t complain.

Overall would recommend Wah Fung with my eyes closed. They are quite popular at the moment for the right reasons: great food and amazing value. Will definitely be coming back to try the other meats soon.

docs.title: Review of Wah Fung No.1 Fast Food
docs.text:
Google review of Wah Fung No.1 Fast Food (5 out of 5, by KBRIN347, 8 months ago): We did a cheap-eats food crawl through the historically rich streets of NYC’s Chinatown, and Wah Fung No. 1 Fast Food absolutely earned its name. This is a cash-only spot, and you should expect to wait at least 20 minutes in line, but the payoff is worth every second. The roast pork and duck are incredibly flavorful, tender, and satisfying. We asked for extra sauce, and that was the right decision. Do not skip that step.

The value here is unmatched. You can get a small lunch plate for just $6, which comes with a generous portion of rice, steamed cabbage, and your choice of roast pork, duck, or chicken. We ordered the large plate with all three meats, shared it between the two of us, and still had leftovers for later that evening.

One important note: if you order the roast duck, eat carefully. The duck is chopped into bite-sized pieces with the bone still inside, so be sure to eat slowly and stay aware.

If you’re anywhere near Chinatown or doing a historic food crawl of NYC’s best cheap eats, Wah Fung should absolutely be on your list. Incredible food, unbeatable prices, and a true New York experience.

docs.title: Review of Wah Fung No.1 Fast Food
docs.text:
Google review of Wah Fung No.1 Fast Food (4 out of 5, by Connie Kwok, 5 months ago): CASH ONLY. This spot is all about no‑frills standard Cantonese roast meats. The menu is simple — roast pork, roast duck, or chicken over white rice with steamed napa cabbage — and both the small and large come packed to the brim.

I got the roast pork and roast duck combo. The duck was the standout: tender, flavorful, and easily what I’d order on its own next time. The pork was average- prefer my roast pork on the fattier side, so it wasn’t as juicy or flavorful as other places nearby. I also skipped the sauce (personal preference), though the standard is sauce on top.

What really impressed me was the efficiency. The two guys working were cutting, packing, and taking cash in a rhythm that kept the line moving, and they were meticulous about changing gloves every time they handled money. Small detail, big impact.

It’s cash only, strictly takeout, and the shop is tiny — maybe four people can stand inside — so plan ahead, especially in bad weather. I waited about 20 minutes with around 10 people ahead of me, and the line doubled by the time I left.

Simple, satisfying, great value. And with Sara D. Roosevelt Park right across the street, it’s the perfect spot to take your meal and enjoy it outside!

Google review of Golden Unicorn (4 out of 5, by Leonard Lim, 4 months ago): Visited Golden Unicorn during our trip to New York City. The restaurant is spacious, lively, and has the classic dim sum atmosphere that is becoming harder to find nowadays.

The dim sum was generally acceptable, especially considering we were dining in NYC. Service was efficient, and there was a good variety of dishes available. However, having traveled extensively in Asia, we felt the quality and refinement of the dim sum did not quite match what you can find in places such as Hong Kong, Singapore, or Guangzhou.

That said, Golden Unicorn remains a solid option for those looking to enjoy traditional Cantonese dim sum in Chinatown. A pleasant experience overall, but expectations should be adjusted if you’re accustomed to top-tier dim sum in Asia.

As for the dim sum itself, I’d say it was good, though not the best I’ve ever had. I’ve definitely had better elsewhere. But the porridge alone made this place memorable for me.

Google review of McDonald's (1 out of 5, by RoRo, 6 months ago): I visited this location during my first trip to New York, hoping to use up some loose change and have a simple order. A small tea with hot water and a tea bag. I placed my order at the kiosk, intending to pay in cash, but I wasn’t familiar with how to use the cash machine. So I went to the counter to ask for help and pay directly.
I waited at the front for about 10 minutes, trying not to be a bother, as the cashier seemed busy and not very approachable. When I finally asked for assistance, I was told to go to the machine in the back. I explained that I was having difficulty and just wanted to pay cash for my order (I had the exact amount, $1.62), but instead of helping, she pointed to the work behind her and said she had too much to do.
I completely understand that fast food environments can be busy and demanding. I wasn’t expecting exceptional service, but I was honestly surprised by how dismissive the interaction felt. A little guidance or basic courtesy would have made a big difference.
To be honest, the experience left me feeling so unwelcome that I couldn’t help but think it might have been better to just toss my $1.62 into a fountain and make a wish instead.
As a first-time visitor to New York, this was quite disappointing.

docs.title: Review of Chick-fil-A
docs.text:
Google review of Chick-fil-A (5 out of 5, by Department of Place Ratings, 6 months ago): Chick-fil-A is the fast food chain that closes on Sundays and still beats every place that stays open all 7 days. That alone says everything.
The sandwich is simple but perfectly executed. Pickle-juice marinated chicken breast, breaded and fried, on a buttered brioche bun. Juicy inside, crispy outside. No mystery fillers. The Spicy Deluxe is for people with actual personality.
The service is absurdly good for fast food. They say "my pleasure" and they mean it. The drive-thru has people outside with tablets taking orders in real time, the most efficient in the industry. You feel like a customer, not a number.
The nuggets are real breast meat, no mechanically separated mystery chicken. The Waffle Fries hold their salt perfectly. The sauces, especially the Chick-fil-A Sauce and Polynesian, are reason enough to go on their own.
But the best part, and there is no debate, is the Frosted Lemonade. Freshly squeezed lemonade blended with soft-serve vanilla ice cream. Creamy, tangy, cold, and sweet all at once. No fast food drink comes close. If you walk into a Chick-fil-A and don't order the Frosted Lemonade, you basically wasted the trip.

docs.text: Google review of Chick-fil-A (1 out of 5, by Ben Shaw, 3 months ago): The floor manager needs to be fired. He does not have the right personality for Chick-fil-A. Incredibly rude. We came in for Cow Appreciation Day dressed up in black and white, with printed cow-themed accessories and even a cow bell. We clearly put in effort and were there in the spirit of the event. The server was ready to honor the promotion, but the floor manager stepped in, read the official memo out loud to us, and refused because we didn’t have a cow mask. Technicality aside, the way he handled it was condescending and dismissive. No apology, no small gesture like a free drink, nothing. Just a lecture. This is supposed to be a fun event that builds goodwill, and he managed to turn it into an embarrassing experience. Every other Chick-fil-A employee I’ve encountered understands hospitality. This guy does not. One star.

Visiting the One World Observatory was, without a doubt, one of the highlights of my entire trip. From the moment I arrived, I was impressed by the warmth and professionalism of every single staff member..  from the security team at the entrance to the floor guides at the top. Everyone made me feel genuinely welcomed and well taken care of.

But the real highlight? The view. There are no words that can truly do it justice ..you simply have to be there to feel the emotion. Standing above New York City, watching the skyline stretch endlessly in every direction, is the kind of moment that stays with you forever.

I give it a perfect 10 out of 10. Absolutely worth every second. If you ever have the chance to visit, don't hesitate .... go.

Every visit feels satisfying, whether I’m craving classic tacos, cheesy quesadillas, or their famous Crunchwrap Supreme. The menu is full of creative options, and I love that they constantly introduce new limited-time items that keep things exciting. The staff is always friendly and efficient, making sure orders come out fresh and correct.

docs.title: Review of Taco Bell Cantina
docs.text: Google review of Taco Bell Cantina (1 out of 5, by Aidan Pereira, 5 months ago): I can't speak to how this location runs during the daytime, but i'd definitely advise to never step foot in here late at night. It was an absolute madhouse. Essentially a mosh-pit of shouting, disgruntled delivery couriers, drunk finance people, and spaced-out clubgoers. I was hardly able to walk inside — everyone was packed tightly like sardines. As soon as you frantically do push yourself up to the counter, the employees seem exhausted, as if they're about to drop dead from the sheer volume of orders. Personally, my order took over 30 minutes to come out, and it was both cold and incorrect. And once you actually get your order — don't even think about letting go of it. Many homeless people lurking inside, who will snatch up your food first chance they get (obviously, I don't blame them, but it was a bit overbearing).

docs.text:
Google review of Chipotle Mexican Grill (2 out of 5, by HYEHYUN KIM, a month ago): Short Review

Very disappointing experience. I placed a pickup order for 7:40 PM and had to wait over 10 minutes, even though the store wasn’t busy.

When I got back to my hotel, I discovered that both guacamole ($2.95 extra) and the extra fajita vegetables I paid for were completely missing. There wasn’t even a trace of either item.

Guacamole is one of the main reasons I order Chipotle, so this was especially frustrating. I understand mistakes happen, but customers should not be charged for items they never receive.

I expect a refund for both missing add-ons and an appropriate response from the management.

Google review of Chipotle Mexican Grill (1 out of 5, by Rakesh Patel (Rocky), 2 months ago): Extremely disappointing experience. We came here with a large group of 16 people, and the entire visit was mishandled from start to finish.
First, they were completely out of basic ingredients like fajita peppers and onions, and didn't even have any hot sauce (the spicy one) available. When we politely asked a few questions about the menu, the staff responded by making rude faces, rolling their eyes, and treating us with absolute hostility.
The treatment of customers here is completely unacceptable. Running out of food is one thing, but treating paying customers—especially a large group—with such open disrespect and poor service is awful. Would give zero stars if Google allowed it. Save your money and go somewhere else.

docs.title: Review of Chipotle Mexican Grill
docs.text:
Google review of Chipotle Mexican Grill (1 out of 5, by Keyur Patel, 4 months ago): We visited this Chipotle location around 10 PM, about an hour before closing. Unfortunately, several menu items were unavailable during our visit. When we ordered a veggie bowl, they were out of black beans, sour cream, and guacamole.

After requesting for so long, we were eventually given sour cream, but other items were still not restocked and denied to restock. The overall service felt rushed and inattentive, and there seemed to be reluctance to refill ingredients closer to closing time.

Because of this, we were unable to receive a complete order as expected.

Based on this visit, I would strongly recommend avoiding this location in the evening if you want the full menu and proper service, as availability and attention to orders appear to decline significantly closer to closing time.

docs.title: Review of Chipotle Mexican Grill
docs.text: Google review of Chipotle Mexican Grill (5 out of 5, by Exploring_Food_Places, 9 months ago): This Chipotle is in a great spot—very close to the Wall Street Bull Statue and right along the route to the Staten Island and Statue of Liberty ferries. It’s convenient for a quick meal while sightseeing. There’s plenty of seating, and the street views from all sides make it a nice place to sit and relax. The food was solid overall, though the white rice could use a bit more lemon or salt for extra flavor. Still, a reliable stop in a busy area.

docs.title: Review of Burger King
docs.text:
Google review of Burger King (5 out of 5, by Elle G., 10 months ago): This, my first ever trip to NYC, I stumbled across this location that was made iconic on 9/11.  I appreciate its strength and resilience during that dark and chaotic time.

I stopped in and ordered a Whopper meal.  The order process was made quick and easy with a kiosk at the counter.  It was a bit busy, but I didn’t have a long wait.  My order was accurate and served to me with a smile.  I took my meal to go, so I can’t comment on the dining room upstairs of the very tiny main floor.  There’s a lovely little park/square across the street that was beautifully decorated for the holidays, with lots of lights.  It’s a great spot to sit and enjoy your meal while enjoying the lights.

docs.text: Google review of TLK- Tigerlily Kitchen (TAKEOUT & CATERING) (5 out of 5, by Carlos Deschamps, a year ago): Came here on a date with the wife since I'm allergic to gluten and I got to say this place didn't disappoint! We made a reservation and the environment feels cozy and great for dinner dates. The staff were super nice as well. The food was fantastic from drinks to appetizers. The coconut shrimp was one of the best appetizer I ever had, highly recommend trying them! The Korean Fried Chicken was good and the peanut noodles, overall everything was amazing and you won't go wrong with any choices. Best tasting pop-up restaurant I ever been too.

docs.title: Review of TLK- Tigerlily Kitchen (TAKEOUT & CATERING)
docs.text: Google review of TLK- Tigerlily Kitchen (TAKEOUT & CATERING) (5 out of 5, by Michelle Kahn, a year ago): My friend and I went to their Friday night pop up location and had a delicious meal. The food was all so good and we loved that it was all gluten free. My friend has a gluten allergy and was able to eat everything without concern. Service was great and they even brought me a free dessert for my birthday. We got the coconut shrimp and spicy tuna rice cakes as an appetizer. For entrees, I had the green curry salmon which was cooked perfectly and my friend had the Korean fried chicken which had just enough kick but wasn’t crazy spicy. The space itself is cute, but it’s quite small because it’s their pop up kitchen and not the full restaurant. I believe they are working towards reopening the full restaurant space and I look forward to returning when they do.

docs.title: Review of TLK- Tigerlily Kitchen (TAKEOUT & CATERING)
docs.text:
Google review of TLK- Tigerlily Kitchen (TAKEOUT & CATERING) (5 out of 5, by Benny Conn, 2 years ago): Had a great experience at TLK, we did order things that were mostly quite spicy but everything was so flavorful we couldn’t stop eating even as we were sweating profusely. The ho fun noodles were the biggest culprit but were also probably our favorite dish. We also very much enjoyed the eggplant, was less spicy and had a sort of pickled flavor that was nice, as well as the yucca fries and the spring rolls. The yucca fries looked exactly like regular fries and had a bit of a tougher texture, in the best way possible. I’ll definitely be coming back to enjoy these creative flavors again.

The vibe is also pretty dark and the bar looks nice, this would be a great place to grab some unique drinks as well. I got myself one of the non alcoholic drinks and it showed up in a panda cup which was cute and it was a very creamy coconut drink that I slurped right up.

docs.title: Review of TLK- Tigerlily Kitchen (TAKEOUT & CATERING)
docs.text:
Google review of TLK- Tigerlily Kitchen (TAKEOUT & CATERING) (5 out of 5, by Jessica Duncan, 9 months ago): We used Michelle and TLK to cater our wedding reception. I highly recommend that anybody else who needs catering uses TLK. They are beyond professional. The food was absolutely amazing, guests still rave about it months later. She adjusted the menu so every single guest with allergies was accommodated and we didn't need to worry (guests with nut issues could eat everything). She features gluten free and dairy free food, but honestly, who cares. It is hands down the best wedding catering I've ever had. She also coordinated setup perfectly with our venue. We didn't have to do anything.

11/10 great experience.

docs.title: Review of Yan Wo Dou Bun
docs.text: Google review of Yan Wo Dou Bun (4 out of 5, by Zhong Yang, 7 months ago): Never have tofu pudding this silky smooth, not even in Hong Kong, just need some more soy bean flavor. 😋 Definitely need to visit a Yan Wo in Hong Kong to see if they can top what we have here. I like the pan-fried stuffed eggplant, tofu, and peppers. Will be back to try some other items.

docs.title: Review of Yan Wo Dou Bun
docs.text:
Google review of Yan Wo Dou Bun (4 out of 5, by Kahei Chan, 6 months ago): The tofu pudding was SO soft and silken but the sesame paste was too sweet, and there wasn't enough tofu to balance it out. I would prob try it again just with ginger.

The tofu itself is probably the best I've had in NYC.

docs.title: Review of Yan Wo Dou Bun
docs.text:
Google review of Yan Wo Dou Bun (5 out of 5, by Nick Noronha Rosenbaum, a month ago): I’m shooketh friends, there is truly top tier douhua at this little stall in the Mott St food court. My Malaysian friend and I stopped in on a whim, not expecting much, but wow. The silky, the smooth, the sweet, the savory. I’ve had much worse douhua than this in actual China.

I had black sesame flavor (sooooo good) and my friend opted for the liangfen (grass jelly) with brown sugar syrup, which was good but not as good as the black sesame, now you know. Would be back in a heartbeat.

Plus the old Canto auntie running the stall is so cute and sweet. Go now so you don’t make her cry. Cash only but that keeps it cheap!

docs.title: Review of Yan Wo Dou Bun
docs.text: Google review of Yan Wo Dou Bun (5 out of 5, by Alvin Ho, 6 months ago): The only authentic Hong Kong Tofu dessert in the mall.  Look no further.  Best dark Sesame tofu pudding 芝麻豆腐花

docs.title: Review of Yan Wo Dou Bun
docs.text:
Google review of Yan Wo Dou Bun (4 out of 5, by Jenn L, a year ago): I stopped by for lunch and ordered the three treasures as it was recommended by someone. Also added on a soy milk which comes hot. I had to wait a bit as everything is made to order and there was only one staff member working the stall. I had asked for sugar to be added to my soy milk but I guess they don't add too much as it tasted like unsweetened soymilk. Less sugar is healthier so that's a pro.

The three treasures is basically pan fried vegetables (bell pepper, eggplant and tofu) stuffed with fish paste then topped with soy sauce and hot sauce (adding these sauces definitely made it tastier). It was pretty good value for something that could fill me up and wasn't too expensive. I'll have to give their other dishes a try the next time I visit the food court.

docs.text: Google review of Conwell Coffee & Cocktail Hall (4 out of 5, by Jaye Aster Broder, 5 months ago): The environment is really cool. Staff are friendly and give reliable recommendations. It gets very busy around noon on Saturdays. The coffee and food isn’t timed super well so you may receive one way before the other. We liked the cookie with the coffee. We preferred the French toast to the eggs Benedict. There is some cool seating in a back from with a vault door. I would definitely return here for drinks or brunch.

docs.title: Review of Conwell Coffee & Cocktail Hall
docs.text: Google review of Conwell Coffee & Cocktail Hall (4 out of 5, by Oxana Minchenko, 3 months ago): Superb atmosphere bit wish their service and opening hours were as clear on the website — we came all the way across the city to explore it because friend recommended and found out they the kitchen is closed until 5:30 and we can only have a coffee and a pastry. Almost agreed to that just to enjoy the wonderful art deco atmosphere— but learned that the choose of pastries is sooooo limited so I can’t really choose anything. I am not that picky, but we decided to come back. But again the interior is incredible and I heard that there are live music performances there. Surprised to have such a lean choice at 5pm Saturday.

docs.title: Review of Conwell Coffee & Cocktail Hall
docs.text: Google review of Conwell Coffee & Cocktail Hall (5 out of 5, by Chael MacKinnon Appelbaum, 10 months ago): Loved our dinner here! We went on a double date on a December evening and this was the perfect spot. It is equally cozy as it is spacious, and Conwell boasts a hard-to-come-by amount of table space for New York City. The place was alive and buzzing but it wasn’t loud because there was so much space between tables. We got drinks at the bar first and the French 75s were delightfuuuuul. For an appetizer, we got the tater tots - a little crispier than I usually adore but I still enjoyed. For dinner we got the salmon and the steak sandwich. It was my first time ever trying salmon lol but I was feeling brave and it paid off because I loved it. Def a place to bring someone during the holiday season if they’re in the city visiting! We will be back.

docs.title: Review of Conwell Coffee & Cocktail Hall
docs.text:
Google review of Conwell Coffee & Cocktail Hall (4 out of 5, by Aaron P. Chen, 4 months ago): Last Saturday afternoon, I visited Conwell Coffee Hall, a beautiful Gilded age inspired café tucked in the heart of New York City’s Financial District. Housed inside a grand historic bank building, the space immediately impressed me with its soaring ceilings, elegant marble details, ornate chandeliers, antique lighting, and the dramatic old vault in the back. It truly feels like stepping back in time.
The weekend atmosphere was relaxed and charming, much calmer than the usual weekday rush. I found a comfortable plush couch near the window and settled in for a leisurely brunch. The flaky croissants were some of the best I’ve had, the French toast was rich and perfectly sweet, and my cappuccino was pulled beautifully with rich, smooth flavor. The menu offers elevated café classics at fair prices for the area, and the service was warm and attentive.
Whether you’re people-watching, catching up with friends, or simply enjoying a quiet moment, this place makes you feel transported to another era. It’s the perfect escape from the city’s fast pace.
Highly recommended for anyone looking for a sophisticated yet welcoming weekend spot in FiDi.

docs.title: Review of Conwell Coffee & Cocktail Hall
docs.text: Google review of Conwell Coffee & Cocktail Hall (1 out of 5, by 박소라, 3 months ago): The venue itself has a beautiful, historic atmosphere, but the service was an absolute nightmare. I dropped my knife and spilled my drink all over the table. I tried to call our server twice—they literally looked right at me and just walked past, completely ignoring the mess and my requests. On top of that, they served my bottled cider without even bringing a glass, leaving me to sit at a dirty table until I had to explicitly ask for one myself. When I finally asked for a to-go container for my leftovers, they kept me waiting, claiming it would take 4 minutes just to bring a box. When I left a $1 tip due to this horrific experience, they had the nerve to hand me a separate tip receipt to pressure me, so I wrote exactly why they didn't deserve a tip on it. Beautiful place, but completely ruined by the worst and most unprofessional service I’ve ever experienced in New York. Avoid this place if you expect even a basic level of hospitality.

docs.title: Review of Happy Medium
docs.text:
Google review of Happy Medium (5 out of 5, by Jessica Bachansingh, 4 months ago): Came for a figure drawing class on Tuesday night. Price was $35 and included a paper pad, charcoal to use, and a free NA drink.

The class was a bit shorter than others I’ve been to, but good structure otherwise. At the end they encourage people to put their work in the middle for people to enjoy. I liked that part.

Cozy atmosphere and tons of art setups to sit down and draw at your leisure.

docs.title: Review of Happy Medium
docs.text:
Google review of Happy Medium (5 out of 5, by Plate Cleaner Club, 5 months ago): 🎨✨ Such a fun and unique date night spot in the LES! Happy Medium is the perfect mix of an art studio + cozy café vibe. I went on a Friday night and definitely recommend making a reservation ahead of time since it gets busy. The reservation gives you around 2 hours, which was honestly the perfect amount of time to relax and create something. 🕯️🍷

I love how many different creative options they have: ceramics, painting, collages, oil pastels, pottery, and more. The downstairs feels more like a ceramic studio, while upstairs has the cutest café setup with drop in art sessions. The whole place has such a calming, vibey atmosphere that makes you want to stay forever. ✨

I painted a mug and the staff explained everything super well. They fire it for you afterward, and you can come back later to pick it up, which makes it feel even more special. They also have a great drink selection with both alcoholic and non alcoholic options 🍸☕️

Overall, such a cute Lower East Side spot and one of the most fun experiences I’ve done in NYC recently. Perfect for a date night, girls night, or just doing something creative and different 🎨💛 Would 100% go back!

docs.title: Review of Happy Medium
docs.text:
Google review of Happy Medium (5 out of 5, by Caity Fischer, 8 months ago): Coming here is a MUST. It’s the perfect spot to come alone, with a few friends, or a date. It’s perfect for novices and life long art lovers.

My husband brought me for our first Valentines married. I had the time of my life. The space is beautiful and so conducive to creativity, the staff are friendly, kind, and informative, and the art supply selections are everything you could wish for. Will I be back? YESSSS.

docs.title: Review of Happy Medium
docs.text: Google review of Happy Medium (5 out of 5, by Michelle, 6 months ago): Very fun! You get a menu of choices so everyone in your group can pick their own project. Service was friendly and kind. Would definitely go back. Me and my friend made the collage, my niece did water color and my cousin did charcoal. We all had a wonderful time!

docs.title: Review of Happy Medium
docs.text: Google review of Happy Medium (5 out of 5, by Suzy Thornley, 8 months ago): Happy medium is such a special place. One where you walk in and the creative vibe takes over. With a plethora of options from watercolors to charcoal, painting pottery to collage, there is always something fun to do at the art cafe. If you are interested in a more guided experience, they offer those as well. I have been eyeballing their lamp making and chair making classes as well as their large canvas painting. Happy medium is a lovely place to try something new among creative minds.

docs.title: Review of % Arabica
docs.text:
Google review of % Arabica (4 out of 5, by J J, 8 months ago): We’ve visited % Arabica Dumbo several times, and it’s consistently a lovely place to enjoy coffee.

The café is bright, spacious, and beautifully designed. The Kyoto Latte is excellent—smooth, well-balanced, and always a highlight. The Americano is also quite good. As a Japanese brand, the attention to detail and coffee quality really shows.

One of the most special features of this location is the large window overlooking the world-famous Brooklyn Bridge. It’s a unique and memorable setting that many people come specifically to experience.

There is a corner seating area with an especially nice view, and it naturally attracts a lot of interest. It’s completely understandable that guests want to take photos there. On occasion, we’ve noticed some visitors bringing professional photography equipment and wearing custom or cosplay outfits, using the space primarily for extended photo sessions.

Everyone should feel welcome to enjoy the café, but in a shared seating environment like this, a little courtesy and awareness of others can help ensure that more guests have the opportunity to enjoy both the coffee and the view.

Overall, this is a wonderful café with high-quality coffee and an iconic setting, and we’ll definitely continue coming back. With mutual consideration among customers, the experience can be even more enjoyable for everyone.

Google review of The Chai Spot (2 out of 5, by Aka, 2 months ago): We came to Chai Spot with high hopes as I was craving a good homemade or street style chai. Unfortunately, the chai itself did not live up to our expectations.

We trued their Kashmiri Butter Chai, which was around $10 and traditional cardamom chai around $7 ( excluding tips)
Sadly, both drinks were disappointing. The chai was not served hot, and it lacked the freshness, aroma, and depth of flavor we were hoping for.
It tasted more like a sweetened stale machine made chai rather than a freshly brewed cup.
Considering the price, we felt it was not worth it, and honestly, the chai experience killed the overall mood of the visit.

They do have typical chai time snacks like samosas, biscuits, toasts similar to the kind of street side snacks you would expect to enjoy with tea.

Coming to the ambience of indoor lounging area, it is a shoe free space, so you have to remove your shoes and leave them on the shoe rack before entering.
Inside, the setup is very unique and relaxed, with floor cushions, low seating, colorful carpets, vibrant fabrics, mirrors, and cozy lounging areas.
You can sit comfortably on the floor cushions or lounging sofa. People were lying down and it felt kind of make out/ private space rather than typical cafe.

They also have books, indoor games, and card games. The vibe is very artistic, and dreamy more like a creative lounge than a regular café.

Overall, I think Chai Spot is charging more for the ambience and experience rather than the chai itself. If you want a unique, colorful lounge to sit, chat, or spend time with friends, you may enjoy the atmosphere. But if you are visiting specifically for authentic, flavorful chai, this place may leave you disappointed

Google review of Manjul Coffee & Clothing (5 out of 5, by Aaron P. Chen, 3 months ago): I had heard about Manjul Coffee for quite some time, and finally had the chance to visit.

I started with a single-origin coffee from Colombia (Jair Arles Galindez, washed Pink Bourbon). The cup was remarkably articulat + bright lemon zest acidity unfolding into layers of blueberry sweetness, followed by a delicate hibiscus like finish. Every note felt clean, precise, and beautifully structured. Love it!!

I then moved on to a single-origin espresso from Ethiopia (Hamasho Adnan). It offered a very different expression: a vivid peach iced tea like sweetness, underpinned by cocoa depth and lifted by blueberry fruit tones. Despite its intensity, the espresso remained exceptionally clean and transparent in structure.

Both cups were genuinely stunning, so much so that this easily stands as one of the most memorable in-café coffee experiences I’ve had in 2025.

The space itself further elevates the experience: calm, understated, and inviting, making it the kind of place where time slows down without you noticing. A café worth returning to, deliberately and often.

Google review of Manjul Coffee & Clothing (5 out of 5, by jared ng, 6 months ago): Wow, what can I say. Amazing coffee, knowledgeable baristas who are great to have a conversation with, in a beautifully modern wood aesthetic space. On a trip here I went not once, not twice but three times within five days. You obviously see the beautiful aesthetic so let me share my experience.

I had Eric and Josh as the baristas I got to know by name. I asked questions and wanted their take on the drinks available and the beans they had from Sey in Brooklyn. They were both really approachable and knowledgeable. Had a long conversation with Eric on brew techniques, coffee brewing toys, and even some general visiting info on where to eat. Josh was really genuine and remembered me by name even though it was a few days in between visits.

I had their drip batch brew (albeit freshly made) and two different pour overs (Gesha and a Rwanda natural process). The Gesha ended up tasting a bit flatter but the Rwanda was beautifully done. The ceramic glass and pour was a beautiful aesthetic touch.

My wife had their pineapple foam coffee (which was interesting but a bit sweet for my liking) and a matcha yuzu drink which was refreshing.

The pastries were good and on beautiful plates. It was served room temp and would have been nice reheated.

The space is stunning and lends a sense of peace. Modern Korean/ Asian themed interior and complete with a tree in the middle of the seating area. I wanted to stay for an hour while just drinking coffee and sitting in my thoughts. But alas I have children and after too much chaos we peaced out.

Would highly recommend for your next coffee trip and strike up a conversation with the staff (if they aren’t hella busy)

The food was absolutely delicious, everything tasted fresh and full of flavor. From the moment we arrived, the service was outstanding and they made us feel very welcome.

The atmosphere of the place is spectacular — very cozy and perfect for enjoying a relaxing breakfast. It was definitely a unique experience and a place we would gladly come back to. Highly recommended.

docs.title: Review of Butler
docs.text: Google review of Butler (5 out of 5, by Sanzida Jahan, a month ago): Visited this brunch place last week with my friend and I really enjoyed it. It’s a very pretty aesthetic brunch place if you wanna go on a cute date. I would say the price is a bit on the expensive side but the experience it’s worth it. The staffs were really nice especially the girl who was helping with our orders. Plus you can see The Brooklyn bridge view from there, it’s really close from The Brooklyn bridge. It can be very crowded too especially between 10-12 it’s the busiest so if you don’t like crowds maybe go a bit later. They have outside dining area too if you prefer not to sit inside.

docs.title: Review of Butler
docs.text: Google review of Butler (5 out of 5, by Shri, 9 months ago): A coffee shop that deserves its high rating! We stopped by Butler to have a light snack and coffee. Ample seating. Got the corner table, super aesthetic location and even better delicacies. Tiramisu latte was the best blend of sweet and bitter, and the avocado lemon thyme cake was just phenomenal. Melts in your mouth!! Barista was very sweet.

docs.title: Review of Butler
docs.text:
Google review of Butler (4 out of 5, by Mark Annese, 9 months ago): Cute breakfast spot and very good coffee.
Espresso was strong, smooth and not bitter
Didn’t have the chance to eat at this spot, however breakfast options from diners looked very giod and with generous portions.
Must try again for breakfast.

docs.title: Review of Matcha Cafe Maiko
docs.text: Google review of Matcha Cafe Maiko (4 out of 5, by Anushka Sanil, 4 months ago): Came for the mango sticky rice sundae special and it was amazing! I loved the mango soft serve, and it was topped with fresh mango, sticky rice and coconut cream. Everything complimented each other well and it was a great dessert. We also tried the mango cheesecake which was ok. It didn’t have as prominent of a mango flavor. It’s a cute spot, but small.

docs.title: Review of Matcha Cafe Maiko
docs.text: Google review of Matcha Cafe Maiko (5 out of 5, by Kiwi K, 2 months ago): I got the matcha and ube soft serve the other day, and I loved it! You could really taste the high-quality matcha powder. Then, I went back to try the Dirty Matcha Latte for a caffeine boost. The sweet staff member was so kind and wonderful to chat with.

docs.title: Review of Matcha Cafe Maiko
docs.text:
Google review of Matcha Cafe Maiko (5 out of 5, by Tiffany V, 3 months ago): 5/5 Matcha Mango Soft Serve + Mango Sticky Rice -- loved this month's special! Mango flavor was quite good, very smooth soft serve. Loved the sticky rice. Not too sweet at all!

Wish this location had more seating, only two tables outside.

docs.title: Review of Matcha Cafe Maiko
docs.text:
Google review of Matcha Cafe Maiko (4 out of 5, by Breezy Sling, 6 months ago): Matcha ice cream is one of those treats that feels refreshing with every bite. The natural green color is soothing, the flavor is little toasty and taste lingers in your mouth. It is a dessert that evokes a calming experience with every spoonful.

It is a delicious dessert, but it is also an experience of quiet luxury. Cheers!

docs.title: Review of Matcha Cafe Maiko
docs.text:
Google review of Matcha Cafe Maiko (3 out of 5, by K O, 5 months ago): We ordered the strawberry and banana pudding matcha.

I wish they added some banana pudding at the bottom of the cup so you get that initial taste right away or more of the banana pudding in general.
The strawberry matcha was fine as well.

Was it worth $27 CAD, no. But the drinks were good.

docs.title: Review of Laughing Man Coffee
docs.text: Google review of Laughing Man Coffee (4 out of 5, by Georgia Panagiotakos, 6 months ago): Found my new favorite coffee spot in downtown Manhattan! ☕️ Laughing Man Cafe has the best vibes—don’t miss the giant screen with inspiring quotes that keep you motivated while you sip. The coffee is excellent, the food is fresh, and the service is always friendly. A perfect cozy gem in Tribeca!"

docs.title: Review of Laughing Man Coffee
docs.text:
Google review of Laughing Man Coffee (3 out of 5, by Adam Wilson, 2 months ago): Well being an Australian I thought I would support a fellow country man.
I ordered Avo on toast with poached eggs to have dining in. The food turned up in a paper bag then when I advised it was to have in it was taken away and returned 10 minutes later with fried eggs and a takeaway coffee. No need to let the staff know as they knew and giggled anyway. The coffee was actually good but I won’t be returning unfortunately. If you’re visiting the coffee is worth it hence I gave 3 stars otherwise it would’ve been 1 star. Sorry Hugh

docs.title: Review of Laughing Man Coffee
docs.text: Google review of Laughing Man Coffee (5 out of 5, by yz here, 4 months ago): Great Coffee, Spacious and very modern design, outdoor and indoor seating are plentiful. Such a great place to get a quality coffee drink and a full menu by Slate. We tried today their Oat Milk Date Shake Latte, it was unbelievable! they blend dates with oat milk and mix it with two shots of espresso - it is SO GOOD!!  ask for a cinnamon on top, sit down and enjoy. Highly recommend !!

docs.title: Review of Laughing Man Coffee
docs.text:
Google review of Laughing Man Coffee (5 out of 5, by Ettore Michelin, 11 months ago): If you are in Tribeca, you can't not go to Laughing Man Coffee!

Good coffee, good food, spacious place, and most importantly great people... just a perfect spot for everyone, whether you need to tackle some laptop stuff, have a coffee date/meeting, catch up with a friend, or simply need your daily caffeine dose!

See ya soon :)

docs.title: Review of Laughing Man Coffee
docs.text:
Google review of Laughing Man Coffee (2 out of 5, by Neil Capel, 2 months ago): Terrible flat white. Scalded the milk. Not sure what happened. This used to be one of the best places to get coffee.

(+If you want to make it right maybe don't have AI write the reply....)

docs.title: Review of Urban Backyard - Nolita
docs.text: Google review of Urban Backyard - Nolita (5 out of 5, by Seppy, 5 months ago): Went to grab a coffee to go with our Leon's bagels. I got the lavender latte with oat milk and it was the best lavender latte I've ever had (and that's my usual order if it's on the menu of any coffee shop that I go to). Inside the shop is also SO cute - it looks like a zen garden. Loved the vibes in there. Service was nice and quick. Highly recommend!

docs.title: Review of Urban Backyard - Nolita
docs.text:
Google review of Urban Backyard - Nolita (5 out of 5, by Vianca Martinez, 2 months ago): I ALWAYS END UP COMING BACK TO THIS CAFE WHEN I VISIT NEW YORK!

The tiramisu latte is OUT OF THIS WORLD. And i’ve tried a bunch of this flavored latte.

I also tried their seasonal Yema Latte and that was also delicious.

They have extra seating in the basement and it’s so homey!

docs.title: Review of Urban Backyard - Nolita
docs.text: Google review of Urban Backyard - Nolita (5 out of 5, by Lashay Deloach, 8 months ago): I was so excited to try this cafe when I discovered it on Instagram! The speciality lattes that I wanted to try were out of stock, so I opted for the Tiramisu latte! Goodness, it was so delicious! It was warm to taste! And my sister ate the sugar cookie! Would love to come back again! However, the cafe is quite small!

docs.title: Review of Urban Backyard - Nolita
docs.text: Google review of Urban Backyard - Nolita (5 out of 5, by Y C, 8 months ago): I tried a few of their February specials and everything felt thoughtfully made, not overly sweet or artificial.The Tiramisu Latte was smooth and comforting, especially with the little biscuit on top that made it feel like a drinkable dessert. The Strawberry Matcha Cloud was light and fresh, with real fruit flavor instead of syrupy sweetness. Their Rose Velvet Latte had a subtle floral note that was surprisingly calming. I also loved the Basque cheesecakes, especially the lavender earl grey, which was unique without being overpowering. The space has a warm wood-toned interior that’s perfect for working or catching up with a friend!

docs.title: Review of Urban Backyard - Nolita
docs.text: Google review of Urban Backyard - Nolita (5 out of 5, by Alan Hellawell, a month ago): This “blink-and-you’ll-miss-it” place is one of my FAVORITE cafés in NY. Love the stout paper cups. Enjoyed my hot cappuccino. Beautiful latté art! Very mellow vibe. You really feel insulated from the madding crowd here. Very gentle, mellow staff behind the counter.

docs.title: Review of Rigor Hill Market
docs.text: Google review of Rigor Hill Market (5 out of 5, by Priya, 9 months ago): The hot chocolate was rich, creamy, and absolutely delicious—perfect for anyone who loves a deep, dark chocolate flavor. It’s served warm and topped with marshmallows, which makes it especially comforting during the Christmas season. The cafe is on the smaller side, so plan ahead if you want to dine in. It is a bit pricey, but definitely worth trying at least once.

docs.title: Review of Rigor Hill Market
docs.text: Google review of Rigor Hill Market (5 out of 5, by John Brown, 7 months ago): If you like a thick, creamy dark chocolate hot chocolate, this place is a must go. I wouldn't really consider this a drink. It is a dark chocolate creamy soup with a torched marshmallow in the middle that makes for a perfect snack to warm your soul on the winter. A great take on hot chocolate and a marshmallow that is not to sweet. I recommend getting a drink afterwards because the chocolate is a bit thick on the throat.

docs.title: Review of Rigor Hill Market
docs.text: Google review of Rigor Hill Market (5 out of 5, by Laura Mecier, 9 months ago): Genuinely love this place. Sometimes a bit expensive, but you’re paying for high quality food and great cooking. Every time I’ve come they’ve offered me something more than what i ordered, the staff is easy to talk to, and the food is great. The breakfast sandwich is awesome, salads from the fridge are fresh, the brownie cookie is great, and the hot cocoa is popular for good reason. Love yall!

docs.title: Review of Rigor Hill Market
docs.text: Google review of Rigor Hill Market (3 out of 5, by Lexsy Payr, 10 months ago): For me, it was a very, very, very sweet hot chocolate thick, with almost no milk. I wanted to try the best hot chocolate in NYC, but it didn’t work out. It was expensive and not tasty. Plus, it’s such a small place and there are so many people, especially on weekends

docs.title: Review of Rigor Hill Market
docs.text: Google review of Rigor Hill Market (4 out of 5, by Suriya Govind, 7 months ago): We went to Rigor Hill Market to try their famous hot chocolate. The hot chocolate was perfect - creamy, thick and on the darker side. The toasted marshmallow on top added flavour and the cup felt like a dessert in a cutesy cup. Definitely one of the best hot chocolates we have tried in New York!

docs.title: Review of Stone Street Café
docs.text:
Google review of Stone Street Café (5 out of 5, by Howard “Howie” Tran, a month ago): I will definitely return. The latte was delicious & the banana bread heavenly; & served in/on real dishes. I sat in their lovely back garden with verdant vines & flowering bushes & a whimsical life size horse statue 😆
It’s not far from where I live & I’ll definitely be enjoying this place again. Cheers!

docs.title: Review of Stone Street Café
docs.text: Google review of Stone Street Café (5 out of 5, by Karin D, 6 months ago): Stopped in for breakfast and was pleasantly surprised how nice the atmosphere, people, and food were. Plenty of seating, including a rear patio, and a nice relaxed vibe to the cafe. The coffee was delicious and my kids enjoyed their iced chais. The breakfast burrito was a few steps above your typical breakfast burrito- the fresh avocado accompanied the scrambled eggs and bacon nicely. While a bit pricey for a burrito, it filled me up for hours. The avocado toast was beautifully presented and came with a side salad. My daughter said it was the best she’s had. Great spot for a breakfast, or just a coffee to go.

docs.title: Review of Stone Street Café
docs.text: Google review of Stone Street Café (5 out of 5, by Joyce Lee, 4 months ago): Obsessed with the Bacon Egg & Cheese.  Pancakes & Matcha at Stone Streeet! Love the staff they’re so friendly and the vibes in the courtyard are amazing! Honestly the best place to be on a summers day especially if you want to find a good cafe to work from!  Thank you team!!

docs.title: Review of Stone Street Café
docs.text:
Google review of Stone Street Café (2 out of 5, by Kyle T, 2 months ago): Coffee was good, but the pricing explanation was pretty ridiculous. I ordered an iced cortado and was charged an extra $1 for ice. When I asked why, the barista said it was because the ice machine costs money. I pointed out that the espresso machine and steam wand also cost money, and he responded that the espresso machine is “already here.”

So is the ice machine.

Totally fine if you want to charge more for iced drinks, but just call it what it is: a pricing decision. Trying to justify a $1 ice surcharge based on the cost of the machine makes no sense and left a pretty bad taste for what otherwise seems like a good coffee shop.

docs.title: Review of Stone Street Café
docs.text: Google review of Stone Street Café (5 out of 5, by Mitch Miranda, 5 months ago): The food was fresh and delicious. Don’t let the image fool you this was a lot more filling than it looks. There was little to no wait and it took a little bit for our breakfast to come out, but that’s fine because it was so fresh. Definitely will revisit next time!!!!

docs.title: Review of Harney & Sons SoHo
docs.text: Google review of Harney & Sons SoHo (5 out of 5, by Prabhleen Anand, 3 months ago): Had a wonderful experience at this tea shop in New York! The tea selection was excellent, with plenty of unique flavors to choose from. The staff were friendly, knowledgeable, and happy to help with recommendations. The atmosphere was cozy and relaxing, making it the perfect place to unwind. If you love tea, this shop is definitely worth a visit!

docs.title: Review of Harney & Sons SoHo
docs.text:
Google review of Harney & Sons SoHo (5 out of 5, by Valerie Lima, 7 months ago): So happy we found this place. We were looking for a tea & scones experience, and I’m relieved we didn’t pay $80 per person at one of those “experience” places. My husband found Harney & Sons and discovered they have a mini cafe in the back where you can order a cup of tea (or a flight if you want to try a lot of their teas) and delicious scones!

My husband ordered the Earl Gray flight ($30?) and I got the Cream Tea with earl gray tea ($14!!!!). It was delicious!!!! The scones are served warm and they are perfectly sized with cream and jam. The teas were amazing. Everything we wanted!!!!

docs.title: Review of Harney & Sons SoHo
docs.text:
Google review of Harney & Sons SoHo (5 out of 5, by Kosta Rica, 5 months ago): Huge store.  Like a museum of tea.  Since we are true tea connoisseurs, we have enjoyed this place a lot.
One can get a sample and then get a small bag for $3 to try the tea before fully commuting to it.  Definitely worth a visit!

docs.title: Review of Harney & Sons SoHo
docs.text: Google review of Harney & Sons SoHo (5 out of 5, by FruityEats, 3 months ago): This is like a little hidden gem in SoHo; I’ve been here for to-go refreshments and also partaken in the tea flight with scones. Granted, seating is pretty limited, but the scones were great and the tea flights had a lovely selection.

docs.title: Review of Harney & Sons SoHo
docs.text: Google review of Harney & Sons SoHo (3 out of 5, by Maria R, 3 months ago): Went early on the weekend at opening and there was a line. I got the scones and a iced tea. The scones were declines with the cream and the ice tea was nice and fruity. They have a few different sweeteners and a ton of teas to buy. I also got two loose teas which were good but didnt taste like the names.

docs.title: Review of Butler Bakeshop & Espresso Bar
docs.text:
Google review of Butler Bakeshop & Espresso Bar (5 out of 5, by Julia L., a year ago): ✅ Avocado Toast - amazing and unique spin, with cured peppers and feta, my taste buds were very happy
✅ Overnight Oats - also amazing and unique spin with turmeric, berries, pecans and maple for a lightly sweet taste.

Great cozy & inspiring ambience, music is not too loud which allows for conversation or focused work. Staff is very pleasant!

docs.title: Review of Butler Bakeshop & Espresso Bar
docs.text: Google review of Butler Bakeshop & Espresso Bar (5 out of 5, by Narineh Chase, 3 months ago): my family and i frequently visit new york, and are very picky when it comes to food. we have never gone back anywhere more than once for breakfast… except for here! the food is insanely fresh and wholesome, making us feel like we were eating homemade food. i highly recommend the granola parfait, with in-house made granola. will definitely be back!

docs.title: Review of Butler Bakeshop & Espresso Bar
docs.text: Google review of Butler Bakeshop & Espresso Bar (5 out of 5, by C M, 5 months ago): Not a very big place but the service was quick and exactly as ordered. The matcha was delicious and the avocado toast looked really good! Nice place!

docs.title: Review of Butler Bakeshop & Espresso Bar
docs.text: Google review of Butler Bakeshop & Espresso Bar (5 out of 5, by Peter Mancini, a month ago): We love the coffee and we love the place. Today we got a decaf mocha with almond milk and a carrot cake latte both were spectacular. I’m going to put out a video. Highlighting the spot a little later today. Keep an eye out.

docs.title: Review of Butler Bakeshop & Espresso Bar
docs.text: Google review of Butler Bakeshop & Espresso Bar (4 out of 5, by Andrea Garcia, a year ago): Amazing avocado toast and yogurt bowl. Google review of The Dead Rabbit (4 out of 5, by Renauld “NauldoNation” Brown, 2 months ago): The Dead Rabbit was a solid stop on our trip, but for us, it didn’t quite live up to all the hype. Don’t get me wrong—it’s a good Irish bar with a great atmosphere, and the Guinness was poured well and went down easy.

One thing I did enjoy was looking over the impressive selection of Irish whiskeys displayed on the top shelves. If you’re a whiskey fan, it’s fun just seeing the variety they have behind the bar.

That said, nothing really stood out as being extraordinary. The drinks were good, the service was good, and the atmosphere was enjoyable, but at the end of the day it felt like a really good Irish pub rather than a must-see destination.

I’d still recommend stopping in if you’re in the area or want to check an iconic New York bar off your list. Just go in with realistic expectations. For us, it was a quality Irish pub with great Guinness and a fantastic whiskey selection—not necessarily a place that completely lived up to the legendary reputation.

Google review of Bibliotheque (5 out of 5, by Julian Foster, 3 months ago): Bibliotheque is an absolute gem, especially if you're looking for a comfortable spot to knock out some remote work! The setup is incredibly accommodating—there is tons of comfy seating and lots of accessible outlets so you're never scrambling for a charge. They do cap their (blazing fast) internet connection at 90 minutes, but honestly, that makes total sense. If they didn't, I would probably camp out here for hours, lol.
The drink selection is fantastic. The coffee is genuinely good with plenty of options to choose from, but the real standout for me was the vanilla mimosa—you absolutely have to try it!

Google review of Bibliotheque (4 out of 5, by Deb DelValle, 2 months ago): For a book lover and a wine enthusiast, Bibliothèque NYC was the perfect destination for my friend and me. We had brunch elsewhere beforehand, so our plan was simply to stop in for a glass of wine, a charcuterie board, and to soak in the ambiance and it exceeded our expectations.

From the moment we walked in, we were captivated. The space is absolutely stunning, with books lining the shelves from floor to ceiling. There is seating at the bar in the front, while the back offers a mix of cozy sofas, booths, and tables. If you’d like to enjoy the lounge area in the back, there is a food and beverage minimum, which was perfectly reasonable.

What truly elevated the experience was the exceptional service. Our server warmly welcomed us, asked if it was our first visit, and took the time to walk us through the concept behind the menu. One of the most creative touches was how the wines were organized by literary genres. Just as every genre evokes a different mood, the wines were grouped by flavor profiles inspired by categories like romance, mystery, and thrillers. For those who prefer a more traditional approach, the menu also organizes wines by region. It’s such a clever and thoughtful concept that perfectly complements the library-inspired atmosphere.

Since we’d already eaten, we shared a charcuterie board and enjoyed a glass of wine. The music created a relaxing backdrop, the lighting was warm and intimate, and we loved browsing the titles surrounding us while we talked. The bar was lively and well attended without feeling overwhelming.

Bibliothèque is the kind of place where you can lose track of time. Whether you’re meeting friends, enjoying a date night, or simply looking for a quiet corner to unwind with a great glass of wine, it offers a truly unique atmosphere. I only wish we hadn’t eaten beforehand because there were several menu items I’d love to try next time.

The combination of outstanding service, beautiful design, creative attention to detail, and excellent wine made this a memorable visit. I highly recommend Bibliothèque NYC to anyone who appreciates books, wine, and thoughtfully designed spaces. I’ll definitely be back.

Google review of Overstory (3 out of 5, by Jack Tuggle, 5 months ago): The truth is I moved to New York City about a year and a half ago, and this place has been at the top of the bar list since I've been here. I've been wanting to go for quite a while, but the $70 fee that you must pay to secure a table has been a deterrent for me, just because I get scared whenever I have to put down a card for a table. That's a personal thing.

My friend had a birthday and decided to invite us, and for me it's an automatic yes! I've been wanting to go here for a long time. It's always my goal to visit all the top bars in the city, so we made it happen.

This place is super high up. It takes a while to get to. You have to go up an elevator, up stairs, up stairs, up stairs, and when you finally get there, it's small. It's not a huge place. The table we sat at was tiny. We had five people, but it was fine. We got some snacks. Nothing blew me away when it came to the food. It was good, but I've had much better fried chicken. Everything was crazy expensive. I mean, it's rooftop pricing, what do you expect? All drinks were just okay!

The honest truth is that I didn't really love this place as much as I wanted to. I really wanted to love this place! I'm a sucker for a great bar and a great cocktail. Maybe I'd come back to sit at the bar. Maybe that's a different experience. I just didn't think it was anything special for me. I think I also went during the day time, and I think it's probably better for sunset or night time, and I acknowledge that. The views are amazing, but it was so windy I couldn't even be outside for 2 seconds! So meh, it's fine. I won't go back.

Also, my fears about paying the fee were known. They had booked it for more people. They couldn't come, so we had to eat and drink their fair share. We all had a lot more drinks and food than we really would have had.

The burgers are a bit rare which put my wife off slightly, but I thought they were cooked perfectly (maybe ask for less rare if that bothers you). The mustard was overpowering the poivre sauce which was disappointing, and maybe the bun could be slightly more robust as it did tend to fall apart with the juice. That said, really good, some thing I’d happily come back for. The fries were unreal, coated in some starch to add texture and  crunch, the house made mayo was a perfect dipping sauce. The martinis were great, and the daquiri was good too. Definitely on my list to come back.

Google review of TIME AGAIN (1 out of 5, by Lola Pagola, 5 months ago): Do not go here.

When we first arrived, we grabbed drinks and were looking for a place to stand. One security guard kindly told me to move behind the fenced-off area, so I did. About 30 seconds later, a different security guard came up directly into my face and started yelling, “YOU CAN’T STAND THERE.” I explained that the other security guard had just told me it was okay, but he kept yelling and said he didn’t care. People around us were visibly shocked and even asked if I was okay afterward.

Later in the night, I sat down indoors at a table with my friends. There were already chairs around the table, including one taller chair I happened to be sitting on. Instead of simply telling me the chair wasn’t for seating, an employee aggressively yanked the chair out from underneath me, causing me to fall, and then moved it across the room without saying a word. A simple “Hey, that chair isn’t for sitting” would have been enough and I would have moved immediately.
Completely unacceptable treatment from both security and staff. I’m honestly appalled by how disrespectfully customers are treated here.

Google review of The Highlight Room (1 out of 5, by Jasleen Gill, 2 months ago): If I could give 0 starts I would.

Honestly, one of the worst experiences I’ve had at a NYC venue. The atmosphere may look nice, but the staffs attitude completely ruined the experience.

From the moment we arrived, the staff were incredibly rude, dismissive, and acted like we were inconveniencing them by simply being there. There was absolutely no sense of hospitality or professionalism. The way we were spoken to was unnecessarily condescending, and anytime we tried to ask a question or get assistance, we were met with attitude rather than basic customer service.

For a venue that charges the prices it does, I expected a much higher level of service. Instead, it felt like the staff had no interest in making guests feel welcome or valued. The attitude was especially disappointing considering how much people are paying to spend an evening there.

A nice view and trendy atmosphere mean absolutely nothing when the people working there make you feel uncomfortable and unwelcome. NYC has plenty of rooftop venues with better service and much better hospitality.

Definitely not worth the money or the attitude. I would not recommend it. The only thing I recommend is the owner/management completely re-staffing with appropriate and top tier training.

Google review of Ulysses' (4 out of 5, by Tim Meijer, 5 months ago): We visited this bar and it was a particularly enjoyable experience. The staff were friendly, nothing extraordinary, but simply efficient and attentive. Here, you can have your own little booth where you can sit by the bar. Google review of Ulysses' (4 out of 5, by Nicole C, 2 months ago): After a long shift, a few coworkers and I stopped by Ulysses to try the Monday lobster special we saw on Instagram. Sadly, we got there too late and it was already sold out, but we decided to stick around and have dinner anyway.

The experience was a bit mixed, but overall still pretty good. Two people ordered the fish sandwich with fries. The fries were easily the highlight of the table, crispy and honestly the best part of multiple dishes. The fish itself got mixed reviews: one person said it was kind of lacking flavor, while the other thought it was just okay, nothing special.

Another coworker ordered the steak frites medium, but it came out much closer to rare, like, very rare. That said, it was still flavorful, and once again, the fries carried.

I ordered the chopped iceberg salad without bacon. The portion was great, but it leaned a little watery and could’ve used more seasoning to really bring it together.

Service wise, we did have to ask for silverware, but it looked like the bartender was running the show solo and pretty overwhelmed, so it didn’t feel like a huge deal.

All in all, we’d probably come back just earlier next time so we actually have a shot at that lobster special.

Google review of JIMMY (3 out of 5, by Crystal Santiago, a month ago): The spot itself is really nice and has a great view, but they definitely need a better system for reservations.

We went on 8/29 and arrived a little early for our reservation. There was no one there to check us in or receive us, so we just found a table. We then had to order our drinks at the bar and bring them back ourselves, which feels pretty subpar for a place that charges per person just to enter.

Closer to sunset, someone came over and told us our seats were reserved for another reservation and that we would have to leave soon. We explained that we were actually the ones with the reservation and gave her our name. She never came back, so I assume she confirmed it, but the whole experience just felt disorganized and lacking.

The drinks were also disappointing and way overpriced. I’ve been to cocktail bars all over the world, and this was easily one of the worst in terms of quality for the price.

You’re better off ordering a beer and a shot and enjoying the view, because unfortunately, the view is about all this place is giving.

Google review of 169 Bar (1 out of 5, by Alikhan Virani, 9 months ago): Worst bar in NYC

We were having a great night until a very small accident happened - my friend spilled her drink. She immediately took responsibility and cleaned it up herself. That should have been the end of it.

Instead, two employees chose to humiliate her.

One bartender acted like he was bringing her a fresh beer, then stood behind the bar holding it and made her walk over to get it. When she did, he told her, “It’s the least you could do.” Condescending, unnecessary, and unprofessional.

Then another male staff member approached and called her the c-word in front of other customers, raising his voice and making a scene over something that had already been handled. Watching a grown man verbally attack a woman like that inside a bar was shocking and completely unacceptable.

No one deserves to be treated that way, especially by people whose job is hospitality.

After reading other reviews, it’s clear this is not an isolated incident. There are multiple reports of staff yelling at and degrading patrons, which means management is allowing this culture to continue.

There are too many good bars in Manhattan to waste your time or money at one that treats women with this level of disrespect. We won’t be back.

She said yes, but that I had to sit in a specific corner (least desirable seat in the house), which seemed fair.

After I got my Coke and started eating, she came over and, very rudely, told me I had to leave if I wanted to eat. I don’t understand why I was directed to that table in the first place if I wasn’t actually allowed to eat there, surely not because I wasn’t getting food… it’s a bar and half the people there were just having a drink.

What made it even stranger was that about half the tables were empty, and many other customers were only having drinks, so it didn’t seem like a capacity issue. Being placed in an isolated corner made no sense.

The biggest issue, though, was how I was spoken to. It was clear there had been a misunderstanding, and a polite clarification would have been more than enough. Instead, the interaction came across as unnecessarily rude and left a very negative impression. The rest of the staff seemed perfectly friendly.

Google review of Cool Wine & Spirits (5 out of 5, by Otto Placik, 3 years ago): Amazing place. Tiny, chic and friendly. I literally called 8 stores in NYC about any available Chartreuse knowing it was a rare find. Most stores copped and attitude: "check our website!", " Don't you know that's impossible to get right now" or " I've heard that there might be a store in Brooklyn that may have it, but you're crazy if you think can get it on the island." Well the staff in this tiny shop could not have been more friendly or personable. She said: "For sure, we've got a 375ml green and a 750ml yellow but there's a fantastic new local comparable concoction Faccia Brutto Centerbe that you have to try!".
I made it there pronto. She was amicable and unpretentious.
I bought all 3. She said let me know about your taste test.
Well the Centerbe was close but as my wife described the Green Chartreuse was "thicker and stickier" (probably the honey) and has a 55%ABV vs the 45%ABV but it was close and would easily serve as a good substitute minus the possible Wormwood??????.
This was one of the smallest, coolest shops with a great vibe and amazing customer service. Kudos!!!!

docs.text:
Google review of Michael Towne Wines & Spirits (1 out of 5, by Shanelle R, a year ago): My husband had an extremely disappointing and uncomfortable experience at this store. My husband went in to pick up a large order of Veuve cliquot that had been placed over the phone for a friend’s championship celebration. He provided his ID and credit card to the cashier without issue.

However, another man — who was supposedly  the owner — repeatedly double-checked his credentials, even after they had already been verified by the cashier. This unnecessary and prolonged scrutiny made my husband feel not only racially profiled but also criminalized. When my husband politely asked why his ID and card were being checked again, the “owner” offered no explanation, the cashier seeing the tension and tried to mitigate it proceeded to say “there had been fraud in the past and he’s just being careful”. He then proceeded to ask if he had cash instead. If my card isn’t good, then my money shouldn’t be either, right?

Instead of addressing the concern respectfully, the so called owner dismissed my husband’s question, told him he could leave if he didn’t like it, and claimed he “knew everyone in the neighborhood.” He had no problem leaving. Why do business where your money isn’t wanted. It’s NYC, there are millions of wine and spirits stores. My husband left and was treated better at another establishment.

That kind of attitude is both unprofessional and unacceptable. Customers should be treated with courtesy, not suspicion or hostility. What should have been a simple purchase of high-end champagne turned into a humiliating and frustrating situation. Profiling and treating paying customers this way is unacceptable in 2025. We will never return, and we would strongly caution others about shopping here. Wish I could’ve given it zero stars.
