docs.title: Review of Battery Park Veterinary Hospital
docs.text:
Google review of Battery Park Veterinary Hospital (5 out of 5, by kara Sheldon, 5 months ago): I adopted my puppy MJ in July from a mill situation, so she came with quite a few medical needs. As a stay-at-home wife, she truly feels like my child, and I made it my mission to get her healthy and thriving. I also spent a lot of time researching the right timing for her spay and chose to wait until after her first heat cycle. While I’m very happy with that decision, I would only recommend it to others if you have the time and attention to closely monitor every subtle change in your dog. It really matters for timing things correctly.

This pet hospital has been a complete breath of fresh air and a huge source of relief throughout the entire process. From the day I brought MJ home, they’ve supported us through everything. After 8 to 9 months of care, my puppy is now healthy, happy, and thriving. Her spay was timed perfectly, and her recovery has been smooth.

Dr. LoPresti has helped us through so many issues, from Giardia to a UTI and everything in between. She always meets my concerns with empathy and never once made me feel like I was overreacting for bringing MJ in. That level of care means everything as a dog owner.

Dr. Lin is incredible when it comes to surgery. When we got MJ back after her spay, and removal of a not so great looking mole on her lip, my husband actually joked about whether she was even spayed because the stitching was so clean and well done. She also gave me thoughtful guidance on waiting three months after MJ’s last heat cycle to ensure her hormones were stable before proceeding.

I truly trust this team and feel so lucky to have found them. They’ve played a huge role in giving MJ the healthy, happy life she has today. Highly recommend.

docs.title: Review of Water4Dogs Rehabilitation Center
docs.text:
Google review of Water4Dogs Rehabilitation Center (1 out of 5, by Sam, 2 months ago): REPOSTING - last review was deleted.

We had a really bad experience for our first session and I pulled our dog out in the middle of it. I was actually surprised that no one on staff ever reached out about it. We used to bring our old dog there in 2018 and had an all around great experience, so this threw me for a loop.

While we were waiting for the first therapist we saw the second water treatment therapist treat another human client (who was in the water treatment before us) disrespectfully and rudely; in addition, she was really rough with the elderly dog that came in before us.

When it was our turn for water treatment (treadmill) the therapist took our dog inside the room and I told her from the door to make sure to take off her collar because it rusts and she was extremely rude in her response, saying loudly "get away from the door, you're not allowed in here". The front desk person ended up relaying my message to the therapist who said "everything comes off". Really bad attitude, but I still did not say anything. As she began the treatment I was watching through the window and she told me I could not watch and I told her I was not comfortable with that, as I would like to see what she is doing. After another minute she came out of the treadmill and opened the door to say that I could not watch because she has to create a rapport with the dog, at which point I said "OK forget it, this is not working, pull her out". What about creating a trusting rapport with the humans? The dogs cannot talk or consent, so it is all our responsibility to the best we can by them, and I felt that this was not a good situation.

The largest difference between our previous experience and this one was communication - in 2018 the therapists went through EVERYTHING with us - from explaining why they were doing certain treatments and how they were isolating certain muscles, to showing us how to do certain treatments, as well as making us a part of those treatments, which was a benefit to us as well as our dog. We were able to bring that knowledge back home for PT at home and felt confident every step of the way.

With this last experience, we did not feel confident at any point of the process - we were left in the dark from the very start of therapy and on top of that treated rudely by the very person who is supposed to be caring for our animal. It did not feel good.

On top of everything, no one EVER addressed what had happened - I called numerous times and emailed as well (ALWAYS in a nice tone, I was hoping to rectify the situation and hoping this was a one time occurrence - someone having a bad day). No one ever called me back or responded.

So here we are.

Google review of Biscuits & Bath - Financial District (5 out of 5, by Xinyi He, a year ago): A very long review coming—but definitely worth the read if you’re looking for a place to drop off your dog while at work!

I feel incredibly lucky to have found Biscuits and Bath in the Financial District. I work at the Trinity Building, so the location couldn’t be more convenient. My golden retriever, Noble, absolutely loves it here—and honestly, so do I.

From day one, the staff have treated Noble like family. Everyone is super friendly, patient, and it’s clear how much they genuinely care about every dog. They even send updates (and the cutest photos!) throughout the day, which always brightens mine.

One of my favorite features is the live cameras—I can check in on Noble anytime and watch her play, explore, or nap. Seeing her happy and engaged while I’m at work gives me total peace of mind. She used to have some separation anxiety, but now she sprints to the door the moment she realizes where we’re headed.

The space is indoor-only, which is a huge plus year-round. It’s always spotless, safe, and thoughtfully designed for dogs’ comfort and fun.

She comes home every day happy, tired, and completely content. If you’re looking for a trustworthy, loving, and professionally run daycare for your pup, this is it. Noble and I couldn’t recommend it more!

docs.title: Review of Biscuits & Bath - Financial District
docs.text:
Google review of Biscuits & Bath - Financial District (5 out of 5, by Andrele Victor, 3 months ago): This is a long review, but bear with me, B&B FiDi deserves every word.

My husband and I are first-time dog parents, and we've been bringing our rescue pup, Leia, to Biscuits & Bath FiDi for almost a year.

Leia is a Labrador Retriever mix with major anxiety. When we adopted her, she was terrified of people and very skeptical of other dogs. We were nervous about daycare and didn't know what to expect.

The first person we met was Kelsey, the evening manager. Even though she was closing for the day, she welcomed us in, answered all of our questions, and spent time getting to know Leia. She also told us about all the services B&B offers. Including training, daycare, boarding, grooming, and vet care (which we hadn't realized). Her patience and kindness gave us the confidence to schedule Leia's first daycare visit.

On that first day, Leia was hesitant to come inside after hearing the other dogs barking. The FiDi team gave her encouragement and reassurance that she eventually walked in on her own. We left her there for about five hours, and I'll admit I took several "casual" walks past the playroom windows to check on her. When we picked her up, she didn't want to leave. Kelsey, Paul, and Lesse told us all about the friends she had made and how well she had done.

From then on, Leia adored daycare. There were days she would pull us toward B&B on our walks because she wanted to go see her friends. Having the flexibility to do drop-offs without scheduling was incredibly helpful, and the team always welcomed her with so much love.

What means the most to us is the relationship they've built with Leia. Even after we moved out of the city, she still remembers exactly where B&B FiDi is. She jumps into Paul's arms, gives Lesse kisses, and greets Kelsey with full-body wiggels. That kind of excitement says everything about how she's treated there.

The entire staff has always been kind, patient, and understanding. Whether we needed a last-minute daycare visit or were running late for pickup. They have never made us feel like an inconvenience. More importantly, they have always treated Leia like family.

We're sad we don't get to visit as often now that we've moved, but we'll always be grateful for the love and care they gave our Princess Leia. B&B FiDi is truly one of a kind.

A heartfelt thank you to Kelsey, Paul, Lesse, the groomer (who was so patient with Leia's fear of the dryer), and everyone else at FiDi. I wish I could remember every name, but every single person we've met has been wonderful. Thank you for giving Leia a second home.

📍 503 Broadway, New York, NY 10012

This is hands-down my favorite Zara location in the city. The store is huge, super clean, and always well-stocked with a great variety of clothes, including trendy seasonal pieces and classic staples. If you’re a Zara lover, this one is worth the visit.

What really makes the SoHo location stand out for me is how organized it is. Unlike some other Zara stores in NYC that can feel chaotic, this one has a separate line for purchases and returns, which makes everything so much smoother. I went on a weekend and was pleasantly surprised that the line to check out moved quickly.

The layout is spacious, and the fitting rooms were open and functioning, which is not always the case in busy Manhattan locations.

• Separate return and purchase lines (huge plus!)

Google review of ZARA (4 out of 5, by Raquel Gerlani, a year ago): Great location and spacious layout, but long checkout lines

I recently visited the Zara at 222 Broadway (Financial District), right next to St. Paul’s Chapel and the Fulton Transit Center. It’s super easy to get to, whether you’re walking or hopping off the 4/5/6, R or PATH trains  ￼.

This Zara is huge—around three floors—and the layout feels modern and well-organized, especially upstairs where it’s brighter and more open  ￼. The staff seem low in number, though: the checkout area splits the space in half, and my line wound tightly through the store—felt especially cramped during a weekday lunch rush ().

👍 Pros:
•	Convenient FiDi location at 222 Broadway, Financial District  ￼
•	Three spacious floors stocked with the new seasonal collection ($20–200 range)  ￼
•	Modern design, self-checkout options, and pickup services via the app  ￼

👎 Cons:
•	Long lines at registers—especially around midday on weekdays  ￼
•	Some shoppers noted inconsistent sizing across items  ￼

📅 Hours (subject to change):
•	Mon–Tue: 10 AM – 8 PM
•	Wed–Thu: up to 9 PM
•	Sun: 10 AM – 8 PM  ￼
(Waze lists slightly varied times—Mon–Fri 9:30 AM–9 PM; Sat 10 AM–9 PM; Sun 11 AM–8 PM ().)

⸻

🛍️ Final take:

A stylish, well-stocked Zara in a super accessible spot—perfect for grabbing office-friendly pieces or weekend outfits. Just be prepared for possible wait times at checkout. If you’re quick and catch it off‑peak, it’s a solid shopping stop in FiDi!

Google review of Patagonia (1 out of 5, by isac R, 3 months ago): All of the employees at this store are incredibly friendly, warm, and helpful, except for one person.

There is one older woman, probably in her mid-to-late 60s with white hair, who consistently comes across as rude, condescending, and unpleasant. The way she speaks to customers feels less like customer service and more like she’s lecturing or trying to teach a class. She talks down to people as if she’s correcting them rather than helping them.

What makes it even more frustrating is that she often inserts herself into situations where nobody asked for her assistance. On multiple occasions, she has followed me around and continued giving unsolicited advice even after I showed no interest in engaging with her. It completely ruins what would otherwise be an enjoyable shopping experience.

One of my girl friend had a similar experience. While she was simply trying on different items, this employee made her feel as though she was being treated with suspicion, almost like she was being viewed as a potential shoplifter. My friend  was so uncomfortable that she decided to leave the store altogether.

I honestly don’t understand why someone with such poor customer-service skills is in a customer-facing sales position. One negative interaction with her is enough to drive customers away and discourage purchases. She may mean well, but her approach is intrusive, patronizing, and off-putting. Every other employee at this store has been wonderful, which only makes her behavior stand out even more.

Unfortunately, because of her, what should have been a pleasant shopping experience turned into a very uncomfortable one.

Frankly, I believe she is hurting the store’s business rather than helping it. A sales associate should make customers feel welcome and comfortable, not judged, monitored, or lectured

docs.title: Review of PacSun
docs.text:
Google review of PacSun (1 out of 5, by Ana Milena Quintero Remolina, 4 months ago): At the end of the school year, my son and his friends wanted to spend a day in New York City shopping at some popular stores, including PacSun.

Our group consisted of 12 kids and 3 parents, and we were all looking forward to a fun end-of-year trip. Everything was going well until we visited the store for a second time.

A security guard named Lasha, stepped in front of four girls and one boy, all between 13 and 14 years old, and refused to let them enter. The parents were waiting outside with the shopping bags, so we initially thought the issue might be related to the bags. To avoid any problems, we kept all of the bags with us.

The kids were then allowed back into the store, except for my son, who was singled out and denied entry again. This was his first experience with the brand, and he had genuinely fallen in love with the clothing. He wanted to purchase a pair of shorts, so I decided to accompany him into the store.

At that point, the security guard stepped in front of us and began speaking to us in a loud and confrontational manner in front of other customers and parents who were waiting outside. It was an extremely unpleasant, embarrassing, and uncomfortable experience for both my son and me.

I understand that the kids were excited and may have been talking loudly, but the security guard’s reaction was completely disproportionate to the situation. The level of humiliation was unnecessary and unprofessional.

As a result, several of the kids became afraid to enter the store again. My son was eventually able to go inside only because I accompanied him.

I would also like to acknowledge the store manager, who handled the situation professionally and listened to our concerns. He agreed that the kids were being loud, but he was understanding and respectful throughout the conversation.

Despite the experience, my son purchased two shirts during our first visit and two pairs of shorts during the second visit. The store even offered us a discount, but my son was so uncomfortable after the incident that he wanted to leave as quickly as possible and avoid any further interaction with the security guard.

While we appreciated the manager’s efforts, the behavior of the security guard left a very negative impression and significantly affected what should have been a memorable and enjoyable shopping experience

Beyond the incident involving my son, I personally witnessed the security guard behaving aggressively toward other customers. Several shoppers were looking through clothing stacks to find their sizes when he abruptly instructed them to take only the items from the top. His tone and demeanor appeared hostile and intimidating rather than helpful.

This was not an isolated interaction directed only at our group. Observing similar behavior toward other customers reinforced my concern that the issue was not simply a misunderstanding, but rather a pattern of conduct that negatively affected the overall shopping environment.

Google review of Acne Studios Greene Street (1 out of 5, by Chien Tsai, 4 months ago): I recently contacted SSENSE regarding a price-match request for the Master-Piece Potential 3WAY Backpack in Navy.

The identical backpack was available from Son of a Stag, a long-established retailer that carries Master-Piece products, at a lower final checkout price. I submitted a price-match inquiry and received a response stating that the request could not be processed because Son of a Stag was "not included in our list of eligible competitors."

The response then outlined the following price-match criteria:

• The retailer must be an authorized seller.
• The same style, size, color, material, and season must be available.
• The item must be sold at full price.
• The final price, including shipping, taxes, and duties, must be lower than the SSENSE checkout price.

What I found difficult to understand was that the reason given for the denial did not appear among the criteria that were subsequently listed.

Based on the response I received, it appears that eligibility may depend not only on the stated criteria, but also on whether a retailer is included on an internal list of approved competitors. If that is the case, I believe it would be helpful for customers if that requirement were disclosed more explicitly.

My concern is not that the request was denied. Retailers are free to define the scope of their price-match programs. Rather, the issue is that a customer can independently verify the criteria that were listed—such as product identity, retailer status, and final checkout price—but cannot determine in advance whether a retailer is considered an eligible competitor.

As a result, I found the process less transparent than expected. Greater clarity regarding which retailers qualify for price matching, or whether an approved-competitor list exists, would make it easier for customers to evaluate whether a request is likely to be considered before submitting it.

This review reflects my personal experience with a specific price-match inquiry and my interpretation of the response I received.

Google review of paloma wool (1 out of 5, by Ceren Topçu-Weigand, 7 months ago): I loved the brand until I had these shopping experiences in NYC. In Europe — both online and through their pop-up stores — I always had great experiences.

TL;DR: First ask whether the item is the last one available before trying it on — especially if you want to buy it immediately.

First time: I wanted to buy a top. It was the last item available, and I wanted to wear it for a special occasion that same night. However, I was told they did not want to sell the last item because they preferred to keep it in the store so that other customers could still try it on. I actually had to argue with the sales associate to be able to buy it. In the end, I got it.

Second time: I went to the store to buy a bag that I liked and wanted to purchase. Again, it was the last item, and just as I was about to pay, the sales associate — although friendly on the surface, but still with a very mean-girl attitude — made sure to point out that they do not sell the last item. They then ordered it for me and told me it would be shipped to my address. It has now been 7 days, and the bag is still stuck in Cincinnati due to customs clearance. At least this is what shop tracking tells me.

I support independent European brands, and I truly admire their aesthetics as well as the courage & operations it takes to open stores in Soho, London, and Barcelona — amazing. However, this is not the kind of shopping experience I want to have, and because of that, I will not shop from their NYC store again.

Google review of Tribeca Paint (1 out of 5, by Krechetovvv, 2 years ago): My recent experience with this store's return policy left me deeply disappointed and surprised. Before purchasing two instruments, I expressed doubts about which one would meet my needs and asked the salesperson about the possibility of returning the one that turned out to be unsuitable. After receiving an affirmative nod, I made the purchase. However, to my surprise, at the time of payment at the checkout, I was not given any warning that the product I was purchasing might not be eligible for return. This contradicts common practice and, as far as I am aware, legal requirements that mandate informing customers about such sales conditions.

Moreover, the store lacked any visible notifications or signs regarding the return policy, further compounding my dissatisfaction. When I returned to refund one of the instruments, which had not even been taken out of its packaging, I was denied without any explanation. This was especially disappointing, considering I had never encountered such problems with this store chain before. It felt as though I was deliberately misled about their return policy, which is unacceptable and creates a sense of deceit. As a result, I was left with an unnecessary product and a loss of trust in this store. I strongly advise against this store for those who value honesty and transparency in return policies to avoid similar unpleasant situations.

Google review of Chase Bank (1 out of 5, by Pei Yun Chung, a year ago): It’s October 29, 2024, and I’m at the 28 Library St. Chase branch, just trying to get a five-year bank statement printed. Should be simple, right? Well, not so fast! They tell me they can’t help because – wait for it – paper is “expensive.”

Now, I’m sitting there, doing some quick mental math. You can get 300 sheets of premium A4 paper, made in the U.S., for around $20 to $30 – that’s including NYC sales tax. Meanwhile, every time I’ve transferred money from Taiwan, Chase has cost me a $50 fee for online international wires. At least ten times! So that’s over $500 in fees. But apparently, printing my statements is going to bankrupt them!

And then, as if it couldn’t get any better, they say they can only send me my statements one year at a time. One year at a time! I mean, come on – my own banking history, and they’re treating it like it’s some rare archival material. Even when I showed them Chase’s own policy, which says I could pay the fee and pick up the statements in the branch, they rejected me anyway – no reason, just a flat-out “no.”

I ask if they can show me the rules that back up these rejections – you know, just a little proof. And what do they come up with? Absolutely nothing. Then, for about 30 minutes, we’re sitting in the meeting room, where two more employees join in, like we’re about to hold a summit on the economics of paper. And guess what? Those employees just as lost as everyone else.

So, no five-year paper statement for me, but I did leave with a solid story about how a hundreds-of-billions dollar bank can’t afford paper… even with NYC sales tax.

Google review of TD Bank (1 out of 5, by Yinglei Li, 2 months ago): One time, I went to TD Bank after making an appointment a month in advance for a specific service. When I arrived and checked in at the counter, the employee told me that he couldn’t find any record of my appointment.

I told him, “That’s impossible. I have a record of the phone call from your bank. Someone from the bank called me and made the appointment with me. She was a Chinese woman who spoke Cantonese, and we confirmed the date and time.”

I had specifically made the appointment in advance because I’m no longer living in New York City. I actually flew back to New York specifically for this appointment.

Then he told me that they might not be able to take care of the service that day.

I was like, “I specifically flew back to New York because I made this appointment a month ago. And now you’re telling me that you can’t do it today? What am I supposed to do about the cost of my round-trip flight?”

He then said he needed to ask some of his colleagues. They talked among themselves for a while, and eventually he came back and told me that there happened to be another customer who was there that day to do the same type of transaction, so they could take me along with that customer and get my business done as well.

I said, “Okay.”

But then they basically just told me to wait there by myself, and I ended up waiting for a very long time.

What really bothered me was how ridiculous the whole situation felt. I had made an appointment a full month in advance. I had confirmed the exact time and location with someone from the bank, and I had even booked a flight back to New York specifically because of that appointment. Yet when I arrived, they told me they couldn’t find my appointment, and then they acted as if they were doing me a favor by letting me tag along with another customer who happened to be doing the same thing that day.

On top of that, I had to sit there and wait for a long time, while everyone acted as if the problem had nothing to do with them. There was no real sense that they understood that this was their mistake or that they were sorry for the inconvenience they had caused me.

The service itself was related to some other important matters, so I absolutely had to get it taken care of that day. Thankfully, I eventually got everything done.

But after I returned home, I was so frustrated by the experience that I decided I was completely done with TD Bank.

I canceled all of my TD Bank accounts, including all the bank accounts and credit cards I had with them. I called customer service, canceled some of the accounts online, and closed everything I could.

It wasn’t just about one bad experience. What really made me angry was the combination of making an appointment a month in advance, flying all the way back to New York specifically for it, having the bank lose the appointment information, and then being treated as though they were doing me a favor by squeezing me into someone else’s appointment.

After that experience, I simply didn’t want to have anything to do with TD Bank anymore.

docs.title: Review of Bank of America Financial Center
docs.text:
Google review of Bank of America Financial Center (1 out of 5, by Y “Y” W, a year ago): 03/04/2025
A scam set up by the bank itself. another group in BoA BK is working with my case. I am a ball kicked around over 7 months and endless!
01/30/2025 The case was withdrawn????                       11/22/2024Update
Today, here again to ask Jeff for help. 10 a.m. to 17:19—-7 hours! seemed like Jeff was determined to solve the issue, even though he was bounced between different sectors.The two of us stayed by the phone without eating. Jeff kept calling and listening to that hold music, repeatedly answering the same questions until he could respond automatically without thinking.

Finally, at around 5 p.m., someone on the other end promised to provide an answer within 24 to 48 hours. Although I’ve heard this before, I’m grateful for Jeff

After leaving the bank, I helped a Turkish tourist who couldn’t speak English to find the subway and took a screenshot of the route map he needed to show to the police. He insisted on giving me a small souvenir (see photo), saying, “Chinese people have a noble mind.” Later, I held my umbrella for an elderly lady in the rain. She was so touched that she hugged me and thanked me in Chinese. These little moments made me happy today.

Next week is Thanksgiving. I believe the America I used to know, which was filled with kindness, mutual help, and love won’t disappear. Wishing everyone a Happy Thanksgiving!💗

———————————————————
If I could, I would give Bank of America a negative rating.

At the end of July 2024,while I was in Chinatown, New York, I received a mobile banking alert saying that I had made a card transaction in Texas, but I had never been to Texas. That day, concerned about my credit card’s security, I requested to cancel the card, which had over $3,000 that I had deposited. I was told the money would be refunded via a check or to my debit card.

Every one to two weeks after that, I went to this Bank of America financial center in Chinatown. During the first three visits, they told me to wait another one or two weeks. After more than a month, I received a letter saying that a check had been sent to me back in April?! Then why didn’t they tell me this during my previous three visits? What’s more ridiculous is that the check was made out to someone with a completely different name, someone I don’t know, and this person had already cashed it! Why was my money written out to someone else? How could this person cash the check which was supposed to be paid to me?

Since then, I’ve repeatedly been told to wait, and each time I’ve had to wait on the phone for at least an hour, explaining the situation to each representative, as if it were the first time I’d ever reported it. No one ever seems to be truly addressing the issue. I at last had to call Bank of America’s Chinese credit card service line, where they promised a response by the end of September, but when I followed up, it was as if nothing had happened.

It has now been almost three months, and I’ve made countless phone calls—some went through,some not, some even hung up by the staff—and I have visited the Chinatown financial center nearly 10 times, with no progress.

They claim to be investigating, but there’s been no real action. Few people are actually doing their jobs. Their inefficiency, incompetence, and lack of concern for customer experience are infuriating and leave me feeling helpless.

If you, as a Chinese, have a choice, I strongly advise you not to choose Bank of America! However, if you’re left with no other options, you can consider the financial center in Chinatown. The overall service attitude here is very good. These star is for Jeff at the New York financial center and Lia from the Bank of America Chinese service line, who both genuinely tried to provide service and to resolve the issue. I especially want to thank Jeff—every time I went to the Chinatown financial center, I sought him out directly. I appreciate his patience in making phone calls on my behalf, even though without much progress.

I’ll update here if they ever return my money.

Google review of Yu & Me Books (3 out of 5, by Derek Ramoutar, 2 months ago): I visited Yu & Me Books because I loved the concept of a bookstore dedicated to showcasing books by Asian authors. It's a charming, thoughtfully curated space with a wonderful selection that highlights a diverse range of Asian voices and stories.

Unfortunately, the customer service left me a bit disappointed. While I was browsing, one of the employees walked by. We made eye contact, and I smiled as a friendly gesture, but she simply looked away without acknowledging me. It wasn't a major issue, but it didn't feel very welcoming.

At checkout, I noticed a sign about a credit card surcharge. Since I was paying with a debit card, I asked if the surcharge still applied. The employee responded with a quick, stern, "It doesn't matter," which came across as abrupt and dismissive. It made the interaction feel less pleasant than it could have been.

Despite that experience, I would still return because I truly appreciate the store's mission and want to support Asian authors and independent bookstores. I just hope future visits include a warmer, more welcoming customer experience to match the wonderful collection of books.

Google review of Mysterious Book Shop (5 out of 5, by happylioneatsprey, a year ago): A superb bookshop which specializes in suspense, mystery, horror, and true crime publications. This store was a "must-visit" on a recent vacation because I'm a bibliophile and these genres are some of my favorites.
Walking into their space you're surrounded by almost every book on these subjects you can imagine! In the center, there is a couch, table, and chairs for shoppers to sample a book before purchasing. However, the real show stopper is that the back wall is dedicated to the consulting detective, Sherlock Holmes. The lefthand corner are all the original texts from Sir Arthur Conan Doyle, and then progress into modern interpretations, and finally puzzles and games based on the deerstalker wearing, pipe smoking sleuth's adventures and I was delighted.
I highly recommend visiting and buying from this small business due to their extensive and impressive selection. They also have the best warning sign for potential shoplifters I've ever seen.

docs.text:
Google review of Midtown Comics Downtown (5 out of 5, by Eternal, 6 months ago): Working so close to the Fulton Street station, the Midtown Comics Downtown location has been my go-to "Wednesday Warrior" refuge for years. It’s always been a reliable spot to duck out of the Financial District madness and lose myself in the long boxes for a bit.

The store has been closed since February 21st for a massive remodel, and honestly, the neighborhood feels a little emptier without it. I really miss that climb up the stairs to find my pull list waiting, but the rumors about the new setup have me hyped. They’re expanding to two full floors and thankfully adding a street-level entrance.

The Grand Re-Opening is set for May 13th, and I can’t wait to see the upgraded space and the expanded selection they’ve been promising. It’s going to be a game-changer for my lunch breaks to have a bigger, better shop right around the corner again. May can't get here soon enough!

I was going to buy a Kate Moss book, and my friend had just bought one of their magazines the day before. I don't think that's the right way to treat anyone, especially not your customers. I always liked going to this particular store because it was the first one I knew since I moved to New York, but I won't be going back because of this woman's rudeness. So disappointing. Just be honest and be good to your customers. What an amazing selection of magazines at the store. But such a terrible experience. I am never going back.

docs.text:
Google review of powerHouse Books (1 out of 5, by Joanne Weaver, 3 months ago): I will never ever shop here again. My brother in law used the employee bathroom by accident and one of the female employees behind the counter (short, slim build, long dark hair) was incredibly rude to him. And on Father’s Day when he’s got kids in tow. What happened to giving people - especially potentially paying customers - the benefit of the doubt? Awful, miserable, little small-minded person. We put back the things we were going to buy as we wouldn’t spend a dime in this place.

Definitely recommend going to one of the plenty of other independent book stores in the city. Their selection is pretty crap here anyway.

docs.title: Review of Joanne Hendricks Cookbooks
docs.text: Google review of Joanne Hendricks Cookbooks (5 out of 5, by Ken Levin, 4 months ago): Joanne Hendricks cookbooks is my favorite shop in NYC. This is a store for hardcore collectors!  She has very rare and very old cookbooks/cookery books and typically in way better condition then I find online. Joanne herself is so incredible sweet and kind.  Ring her first though. She doesn’t always keep regular hours but I contacted her early in the week and we were able to find a time to visit later in the week. Sooo worth the effort.

docs.title: Review of Joanne Hendricks Cookbooks
docs.text:
Google review of Joanne Hendricks Cookbooks (5 out of 5, by Carmen Rubio, 2 years ago): I’ve been meaning to write this review. Last year, I was in NYC and Whenever I travel, I have a few non-negotiable stops, whether it's my first time in a city or not. Among these are visiting a bookstore and an antique shop, always in search of specific books or unique items.

By sheer chance and luck, I ended up at Joanne’s, and it turned out to be the highlight of my visit to New York City.

From the moment you step in, Joanne’s warmth and knowledge draw you in. Hearing the story behind the shop and having her guide you through the selection of a book is an absolute joy. She is not only a good host but also an incredibly fascinating person.

The shop itself is nothing short of magical, offering the best of both worlds. If you're passionate about gastronomy, culinary arts, and their history, this place will leave you daydreaming. For me was inspiring!

I’ll be returning every time I’m in NYC.

docs.text: Google review of Joanne Hendricks Cookbooks (5 out of 5, by Richard E, 2 months ago): Stopped in very briefly today. What a gem! Great source to treat yourself or procure a meaningful gift. Lovely owner.

docs.title: Review of Joanne Hendricks Cookbooks
docs.text: Google review of Joanne Hendricks Cookbooks (5 out of 5, by Fabian, 2 years ago): This place is so cool! The perfect place if you are enthusiastic about cooking. Definitely not cheap, all the books are special. Perfect spot for a nice gift for a chef or friend who loves to cook. They have a large variety of food writing books, really anything related to food or entertaining. It’s a small and cozy shop so just say hi to Joanne and you can spend 15 minutes to look through pretty much every book. Never know what you are going to find!

docs.title: Review of Joanne Hendricks Cookbooks
docs.text: Google review of Joanne Hendricks Cookbooks (5 out of 5, by Julia Pizzolato, 2 years ago): This is, as others have said, a hidden gem in Greenwich. The charm is in its size; the joy is in the incredible selection of historical and collectible cookbooks you'll discover. For a period of time on a Friday afternoon in late April, I had Joanne all to myself and it was pure pleasure. The only thing missing in our visit was a spot of hot tea and a few biscuits. I will be back to visit every time I'm in the city. I could have stayed for hours talking culinary shop with her. She is a delight and a wealth of knowledge!

docs.text: Google review of Words on Warren- Children's bookshop (5 out of 5, by Thomas Hostetler, a month ago): Beautiful children’s book shop. Very clean and organized. Staff were friendly as well! There were plenty of little areas where you could sit down and read books but also be out of the main walking paths. There was also a very comfortable couch about halfway through the store that adults can use to sit for a minute!

docs.title: Review of Words on Warren- Children's bookshop
docs.text: Google review of Words on Warren- Children's bookshop (5 out of 5, by L.J., 3 months ago): Absolutely loved it! It was clean, it was cozy with a touch of the whimsical, and for me as an older reader I was satisfied with the YA section they offered. The staff were so friendly, and I saw them recommending lots of books. They obviously have fans who come often, since their were children that just loved looking at all the books. You should check it out!

docs.title: Review of Words on Warren- Children's bookshop
docs.text: Google review of Words on Warren- Children's bookshop (5 out of 5, by Irene Koo, 10 months ago): This new children’s bookstore is wonderfully cozy, with ample nooks, chairs, and benches that invite families to linger and read together. The book selection is thoughtfully curated across all ages—board books, picture books, titles for new parents, and even young adult reads—featuring many that aren’t easy to find at the library. One standout was the dedicated transportation section that completely captivated my toddler. It’s the kind of place that makes you want to stay far longer than planned. It’s much welcome especially after Barnes & Noble in the area closed.

docs.text: Google review of V MAGAZINE (1 out of 5, by Dara Bryn Shapiro, 2 years ago): I love V Magazine but my last 3 issues did not arrive. I switched from a subscription to purchasing the issues as they come out because I never used to get my subscription. I’d been receiving the individual orders up until January 2024, and I haven’t received a thing since. I actually ordered V147 twice after the first one didn’t come, and the second one didn’t come either. Shopify collected my money but won’t do a thing to help, and neither the email address nor the phone number for V Magazine are in service. I’ve been collecting V Magazine for a reeeeally long time (since issue 63 I think?) and now I’m going to be missing an issue, not to mention I don’t know where to buy future issues. What’s going on here?? I still get emails from V all the time so why can’t I get the magazines i paid for?
